title: Carotid atherosclerosis and aortic stiffness in masters athletes: Multimodality vascular phenotyping from the Master@Heart study.
authors: Rik Pauwels; Christophe Dausin; Ruben De Bosscher; Jarne De Paepe; Youri Bekhuis; Boris Delpire; Kasper Favere; Jürgen Duchenne; Thijs M H Eijsvogels; Peter Sinnaeve; Steven Dymarkowski; Olivier Ghekiere; Tatiana Kuznetsova; Caroline M Van De Heyning; Paul L Van Herck; Tomas Robyns; Lieven Herbots; André La Gerche; Hein Heidbuchel; Rik Willems; Guido Claessen
abstract:
Middle-aged male Masters athletes exhibit a higher burden of coronary atherosclerosis on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) compared with healthy controls. Whether this is accompanied by differences in carotid atherosclerosis or aortic stiffness remains uncertain. We assessed carotid atherosclerosis and aortic stiffness across groups, association between carotid atherosclerosis and coronary disease, and the incremental value of carotid plaque beyond traditional risk factors.
In this cross-sectional analysis of the Master@Heart study, 549 low cardiovascular risk men (median age 55 [50-60] years), including lifelong athletes, late-onset athletes, and healthy controls, underwent vascular phenotyping. Carotid plaque was assessed by ultrasound, aortic stiffness by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (PWV), and coronary atherosclerosis by CCTA. Group differences were assessed using chi-square and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Association between carotid and coronary atherosclerosis was evaluated using regression models. Incremental discriminatory value was assessed using ROC curve analysis.
Prevalence of ≥1 carotid plaque did not differ between lifelong athletes, late-onset athletes, and controls (29.5%vs. 33.2% vs. 27.9%; p = 0.54). Carotid stenosis ≥50% was rare (1.2%-2.7%) and similar across groups (p = 0.54). Median PWV did not differ between groups (p = 0.29). Carotid plaque was associated with coronary atherosclerosis on CCTA. However, adding carotid plaque to traditional risk factors did not improve discrimination of coronary atherosclerosis.
In middle-aged male Masters athletes, excess subclinical coronary atherosclerosis is observed without corresponding differences in carotid plaque or aortic stiffness. Although carotid plaque is associated with coronary atherosclerosis, it does not meaningfully improve risk discrimination beyond traditional risk factors.

title: Arterial tortuosity syndrome with coronary artery involvement in a middle-aged female: A case report.
authors: Prinsa Shrestha; Amin Shah; Saroj Gc; Niraj Kumar Sharma; Aditya Mahaseth; Sanjaya Kumar Shrestha
abstract: Arterial tortuosity syndrome (ATS) is a rare autosomal recessive connective-tissue arteriopathy characterized by diffuse elongation and tortuosity of large and medium-sized arteries. Although it is typically diagnosed during childhood, adult presentation may occur and can be overlooked when overt connective-tissue manifestations are absent; coronary involvement is uncommon but clinically important. A 41-year-old woman presented with a two-week history of exertional substernal chest pain and dyspnea. CT coronary angiography demonstrated marked tortuosity of the left main coronary artery with focal kinking approximately 6.8 mm from its origin and 40-45% luminal stenosis (CAD-RADS 2). Contrast-enhanced CT angiography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis demonstrated generalized arterial elongation and marked tortuosity involving the thoracic aorta, supra-aortic branches, and abdominal aortic branches, together with early branching of the main pulmonary artery, without aneurysm, dissection, or intramural hematoma. Conventional coronary angiography was technically unsuccessful because of severe arterial tortuosity, with unsuccessful catheter advancement and coronary engagement despite radial and subsequent femoral access. The overall clinical and imaging findings were highly suggestive of ATS with coronary involvement, although molecular genetic confirmation was not available. The patient was managed conservatively with vascular risk-factor optimization and structured follow-up, with symptomatic improvement at one month. This case highlights that ATS may present in adulthood with coronary artery tortuosity and focal kinking and emphasizes the importance of recognizing diffuse multi-territory arterial tortuosity on CT. Comprehensive vascular imaging can establish a strong radiological suspicion of ATS, identify coronary involvement and procedural challenges, and guide surveillance even when genetic confirmation is unavailable.

title: Rapid Progression of Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy With Sudden Cardiac Death Within the First Year of Heart Transplantation: A Case Report.
authors: Malcom Dix; Jean-Pierre Iskandar; Lefan He; Mohaned S Serdah; Aditya A Joshi; Anuradha Godishala; Abhishek Chaturvedi; Katherine Kaproth-Joslin; David A Dombroski; YeeAnn Chen; Wendy A Cheruiyot; Ronald Chong-Yik; Ronald G Schwartz; Jeffrey Alexis; Igor Gosev; Katherine L Wood; Sabu Thomas
abstract: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) is a major cause of mortality and morbidity within the first 3 years of heart transplantation (HT). CAV results in progressive coronary artery stenosis and may lead to arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. In some cases, sudden cardiac death represents the initial presentation of CAV, as cardiac denervation blunts anginal symptoms that otherwise could have preceded sudden cardiac death (SCD). Here, we describe the case of a 56-year-old man with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. He underwent left ventricular assist device implantation followed by orthotopic HT. Five months after transplantation, he presented with atypical mid-sternal chest discomfort initially thought to be musculoskeletal in origin. Routine coronary angiography at 12 months revealed severe, diffuse 3-vessel disease consistent with International Society of Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT) CAV-3, and cardiac MRI revealed full thickness delayed enhancement in the inferior wall consistent with infarction. Despite overall preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, he developed polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) with an appropriate shock from a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator (WCD) and was transferred with an intra-aortic balloon pump to a larger transplant center and underwent another heart transplantation. This case highlights rapid CAV progression leading to infarction and arrhythmia despite preserved LVEF, emphasizing the need for enhanced screening with biomarkers and imaging as well as earlier consideration for device-based strategies to prevent sudden cardiac death in high-risk transplant recipients.

title: Achieving Reliable Peripheral Nerve Blockade in Cardiogenic Shock With Distorted Femoral Anatomy: A Case Report.
authors: Mohammed I Hakami; Ayman H Mustafa
abstract: Patients with cardiogenic shock and severe structural heart disease may poorly tolerate both general and neuraxial anesthesia. In selected cases, peripheral nerve blockade may reduce hemodynamic disturbance, but the block must be reliable when pain, sympathetic stimulation, or emergency conversion to general anesthesia could be poorly tolerated. We report a 62-year-old woman with cardiogenic shock, low-flow, low-gradient severe aortic stenosis, advanced dilated cardiomyopathy, pulmonary edema, orthopnea, and active femoral bleeding who required urgent femoral artery and vein repair. General anesthesia and neuraxial anesthesia were considered hazardous. Hematoma and anasarca distorted the femoral anatomy and prevented direct femoral nerve visualization. Combined ultrasound guidance and nerve stimulation were used to support safe needle advancement and functional nerve localization. Surgery proceeded with minimal sedation and without escalation of vasoactive support. This case highlights the role of reliability-focused peripheral nerve blockade when conventional anesthetic options are high risk and regional anatomy is distorted.

title: Construction and implantation of a modified trileaflet polytetrafluoroethylene valved conduit for pulmonary valve replacement.
authors: Abel Getachew; Nikita Zadneulitca; Ashok Muralidaran; Castigliano M Bhamidipati; Yoshio Ootaki
abstract:
Handmade expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) valved conduits have emerged as a durable and cost-effective option for pulmonary valve replacement. We have reported excellent results of trileaflet ePTFE valved conduit and the longest follow-up exceeded 10 years. Technical precision during valve construction and implantation is critical to optimize valve function and conduit geometry, and we recently modified the technique. We report our updated technique and clinical outcomes.
The conduit was constructed intraoperatively on a sterile back table while the patient was being prepared by the anesthesia team. Leaflet dimensions were calculated based on conduit diameter, and leaflets were fashioned with 1 mm extensions at each end to reinforce commissural attachment, then sutured to an ePTFE tube graft using 3 CV-5 sutures with external knot tying. The graft was rotated during construction to ensure accurate leaflet alignment and valve competence was confirmed prior to implantation. During implantation, the main pulmonary artery was divided to optimize conduit geometry, minimizing the posterior conduit length and the graft trimmed in a trapezoidal fashion to reduce tension and improve alignment.
Fifty-four patients received ePTFE valved conduit. Conduit sizes were 18 mm (n = 7), 20 mm (n = 9), 22 mm (n = 1), 24 mm (n = 36), and 28 mm (n = 1). Median follow-up was 1.4 years (maximum, 4.3 years). There was 1 mortality during follow-up due to infectious pseudoaneurysm of the aortic root after Ross procedure. One patient developed severe pulmonary insufficiency after surgery. Recent echocardiography showed no significant pulmonary stenosis, pulmonary insufficiency, or valve deterioration in the remaining patients, and no catheter-based or surgical reinterventions have been required to date.
This refined technique for the construction and implantation of a trileaflet ePTFE valved conduit is simple, reproducible, and yields excellent early hemodynamic results. Attention to leaflet design, commissural security, and conduit geometry may contribute to low early failure rates and favorable valve performance. Longer-term follow-up is ongoing to assess durability.

title: Prenatal diagnosis of mitral-pulmonary intervalvular fibrosa pseudoaneurysm associated with TGA causing severe pulmonary stenosis: A rare case report.
authors: Aliya Kemal Ahsan; Putri Yubbu; Anizah Aishah Rosli
abstract:
Pseudoaneurysm of the mitral-aortic intervalvular fibrosa is a rare and typically acquired cardiac lesion, with congenital forms being exceptionally uncommon, particularly when identified prenatally. We report the case of a 23-year-old gravida 2 woman with one previous history of miscarriage who was referred at 25 weeks' gestation for a fetal intracardiac mass. Fetal echocardiography revealed a cystic echogenic mass at the crux of the heart, consistent with a pseudoaneurysm arising from the mitral-pulmonary intervalvular fibrosa (MPIVF) associated with transposition of the great arteries, causing severe left ventricular outflow tract obstruction or subvalvular pulmonary stenosis. The cardiac lesion was also associated with a large mid-muscular ventricular septal defect alongside a small left ventricle suggestive of single-ventricle physiology. This constellation of findings pointed to a diagnosis of complex cyanotic congenital heart disease with possible ductal-dependent pulmonary circulation. Prenatal diagnosis enabled early parental counseling, planning for delivery at a tertiary cardiac center, and postnatal preparation for prostaglandin therapy and surgical evaluation. This case highlights the importance of recognizing MPIVF pseudoaneurysm in the fetal period, particularly when associated with obstructive physiology or major structural anomalies, and contributes to the limited literature on congenital variants of this condition.
Pseudoaneurysm of the mitral-pulmonary intervalvular fibrosa is an exceptionally rare congenital lesion. Its association with transposition of the great arteries, ventricular septal defect, and left ventricular outflow tract obstruction has important prognostic and surgical implications. Prenatal echocardiography is key for recognition, particularly when there is a cystic or echogenic intracardiac mass with a to-and-fro Doppler flow near the atrioventricular junction. Prenatal echocardiography is crucial for early counseling and planned delivery at a tertiary cardiac center.

title: Low-dose Juglone Attenuates Pressure Overload-Induced Cardiac Hypertrophy through Lys207-dependent FoxO1 activation and Mitochondrial protection.
authors: Hongyu Chen; Zhihao Yang; Cheng Zhang; Chengxin Ge; Yingliang Zhao; Shaopeng Cheng; Yilin Wang; Hao Chen; Can Xu; Dongjin Wang; Jie Yang
abstract: Pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy is characterized by mitochondrial dysfunction and redox imbalance. Here, we investigated the efficacy, safety window, and redox-regulatory mechanism of juglone, a naturally occurring 5-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone. In mice subjected to transverse aortic constriction (TAC), high-dose juglone induced cardiac, hepatic, and renal toxicity, whereas 1mg/kg/day was well tolerated and attenuated cardiac hypertrophy. Juglone also suppressed Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in vitro and preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure and mitochondrial membrane potential, respiration, ATP production, and redox homeostasis. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed that juglone reduced stress-associated cardiomyocyte states and enriched calcium-handling cardiomyocytes. Integrated transcriptomic analyses, Biotin-Juglone pull-down assay, surface plasmon resonance, cellular thermal shift assays, molecular docking, and mutational analyses identified FoxO1 as a functional target of juglone. Juglone engaged the FoxO1 DNA-binding domain in a Lys207-dependent manner, and was associated with FoxO1 deacetylation, nuclear accumulation, and transcriptional activation. Activated FoxO1 induced Sesn3 transcription and restored AMPK phosphorylation at Thr172. Sesn3 silencing markedly attenuated juglone-induced AMPK activation and impaired its protective effects against cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and mitochondrial dysfunction. FoxO1 silencing, FoxO1-K207Q mutation, blockade of FoxO1 deacetylation, or inhibition of FoxO1 transcriptional activity impaired these benefits. Importantly, myocardium from patients with aortic valve stenosis-associated hypertrophy exhibited increased FoxO1 acetylation, reduced cardiomyocyte nuclear FoxO1 localization, decreased Sesn3 expression and AMPK phosphorylation, and increased 4-HNE. Collectively, low-dose juglone attenuates pathological hypertrophy and preserves mitochondrial homeostasis through the FoxO1-Sesn3-AMPK axis, while highlighting the importance of dose-dependent redox effects in determining its therapeutic efficacy and systemic toxicity.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.
authors: Lytfi Krasniqi; Mohanad Hamandi; Poul Erik Mortensen; Henrik Nissen; Patricia A Pellikka; Barry A Borlaug; Oke Gerke; Amal Haujir; Louise Oeksnebjerg Krasniqi; Christian Juhl Terkelsen; Lars Peter Riber; Jordi Sanchez Dahl
abstract:
GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR.
Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death.
Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037).
Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

title: Perioperative B-Cell-Targeted Therapy for High-Risk Valve Surgery in Active Primary Sjögren's Disease.
authors: Bing Li; Lili Pan; Hua Liao
abstract:
Primary Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disease driven by B-cell dysregulation. Clinically significant valvular involvement is uncommon, and evidence guiding perioperative immunomodulation remains limited.
A 59-year-old woman with SjD and severe aortic stenosis required valve replacement. Preoperative evaluation demonstrated active SjD with elevated inflammatory markers and hypergammaglobulinemia. Following multidisciplinary discussion, telitacicept, corticosteroids, and hydroxychloroquine were initiated before surgery. After improvement in inflammatory activity, the patient underwent aortic valve and ascending aorta replacement. Histopathologic examination showed degenerative valvular changes with focal inflammatory cell infiltration. The postoperative course was uneventful, with normal prosthetic valve function at 1-year follow-up.
This case highlights the challenges of managing severe valvular heart disease in patients with active primary SjD and a multidisciplinary perioperative strategy incorporating B-cell-targeted therapy. Although preoperative immunomodulation may have attenuated the histopathologic evidence of immune-mediated valvular involvement, the case offers insights when guidance is limited.

title: Intraoperative ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Complicating Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.
authors: Xunlai Lu; Yuanjia Luo; Fanjing Wang; Wei Cao; Jing Cheng; Peng Lu; Shenrui Xu; Jiachao Luo
abstract:
Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction concurrent with endovascular aneurysm repair for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm is an extremely rare and life-threatening emergency, currently lacking unified clinical guidelines for reference.
A 61-year-old male patient underwent endovascular aneurysm repair for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm and experienced persistent hypotension during the procedure. Postprocedural electrocardiogram and cardiac enzyme tests confirmed acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. The patient underwent emergency coronary angiography, which revealed severe stenosis, followed by successful balloon angioplasty. The patient recovered and was discharged following multidisciplinary postoperative care.
This case demonstrates the management principles for multiple life-threatening complications, where the clinical challenge formed by the huge retroperitoneal hematoma (bleeding risk) and the requirement for antiplatelet therapy after urgent revascularization (ischemic risk) was properly addressed. Through accurate identification, precise intervention, and multidisciplinary team collaboration, the patient was successfully rescued. This case provides a referable practical path for clinical decision-making in similar rare scenarios, highlighting the critical value of individualized treatment strategies.

title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
authors: Rafael Gonzalez-Manzanares; Soledad Ojeda; Ignacio Amat-Santos; Albert Ariza-Solé; Rafael Romaguera; Diego López Otero; Luis Nombela-Franco; Livia Gheorge; Jorge Sanz-Sánchez; Carlos Baladrón Zorita; Ignacio Gallo; Rafael Cobas Paz; Antonio Jesús Muñoz García; Victoria Vilalta; Gabriela Veiga Fernández; Juan Gabriel Córdoba Soriano; Pedro Cepas-Gillén; Miriam Sandín Rollán; Xacobe Flores Ríos; Ricardo Palma-Carbajal; Roberto Martín Reyes; Pablo Avanzas; Sergio García Blas; Juan A Franco-Peláez; Javier Martín Moreiras; José Ramón Gonzalez Juanatey; Nieves Gonzalo; German Calle; José Luis Díez; Sandra Santos-Martínez; Rocío González Ferreiro; Erika Muñoz García; Eduard Fernandez-Nofrerias; Xoan Sanmartín; Gabriela Tirado; Alejandro Gutierrez Barri; Inmaculada González Bermúdez; Xavier Rosselló; Valentín Fuster; Borja Ibáñez; Sergio Raposeiras Roubín
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract:
Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain.
In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year.
Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively; P=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]); P for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin.
Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

title: Impact of prolonged balloon inflation on valve expansion and early clinical outcomes following contemporary balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Francesco Cardaioli; Luca Nai Fovino; Tommaso Fabris; Giulia Masiero; Andrea Panza; Massimo Napodano; Chiara Fraccaro; Francesco Putortì; Giuseppe Tarantini
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
abstract:
Incomplete expansion of balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THVs) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may affect valve performance and durability. Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity.
We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes.
This single-centre study analysed consecutive TAVI patients treated for native tricuspid aortic stenosis with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA THV using a prolonged balloon inflation strategy (8 seconds). Valve expansion was assessed by fluoroscopy at multiple frame levels and compared with three validated reference standards. Results were also descriptively compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique. Clinical and haemodynamic outcomes at 30 days were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria.
A total of 84 patients (mean age 78.8 years, 58% male, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score 3.9%) were included. Prolonged inflation resulted in complete THV expansion at the inflow and outflow levels, with only mild underexpansion (98.5±1.3%) detected at the midframe level when manufacturer-defined nominal values were used as the reference. When compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique, expansion values for the 23, 26, and 29 mm valves were consistently similar or higher, whereas lower expansion was observed for the 20 mm size. Device success was achieved in all cases, with no stroke at 30 days. Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 6% of patients. Haemodynamic performance was favourable (mean gradient 9.2 [interquartile range 7.0-10.3] mmHg at 30 days), with no patients having moderate or severe paravalvular leak.
Prolonged balloon inflation during BE THV deployment is associated with favourable valve expansion, haemodynamic results, and a favourable safety profile, consistent with values reported in double-tap series. If confirmed in larger studies, this strategy may represent a simple alternative to routine double-tap in selected patients.

title: Tracking Active Fibroblast-Mediated Tissue Remodelling in Cardiomyopathies: Translational Insights from FAPI PET Imaging.
authors: Inês Fortuna; Janete Santos; Paula Soeiro; Raquel Machado; Ana Oliveira; Jorge Pereira; Giuseppe Limongelli; Teresa Faria; Elisabete Martins; European Reference Network for Rare, Low-Prevalence, or Complex Diseases of the Heart (ERN GUARD-Heart)
abstract: Myocardial fibrosis is a major pathological component of cardiac remodelling and contributes to ventricular stiffness, impaired myocardial function, heart failure progression, and arrhythmic vulnerability across a broad spectrum of cardiomyopathies. In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), fibrotic remodelling encompasses both diffuse interstitial matrix expansion and focal replacement fibrosis and is closely associated with disease severity and adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), using late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and quantitative parametric mapping, is central to non-invasive myocardial tissue characterization. LGE primarily identifies focal areas of replacement fibrosis and scar, whereas native T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) mapping provide complementary information on diffuse myocardial and interstitial tissue abnormalities, including extracellular matrix expansion. However, these techniques characterize the structural and tissue-level consequences of myocardial injury and remodelling rather than directly visualizing the cellular processes underlying fibroblast activation. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor positron emission tomography (FAPI PET) has emerged as a promising molecular imaging approach for assessing active fibroblast-mediated tissue remodelling. By targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a cell-surface serine protease upregulated in activated fibroblasts and myofibroblasts. FAPI radiotracers may provide a molecular readout of accessible FAP expression that complements structural and tissue characterization by CMR. This review examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying active myocardial remodelling, with particular emphasis on transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)/Smad signalling, fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, FAP expression, and extracellular matrix turnover. We critically evaluate the current clinical evidence for FAPI PET/CT and hybrid PET/CMR across cardiomyopathies, focusing on HCM while also considering ischemic, inflammatory, infiltrative, and other non-ischemic forms of cardiac remodelling. Particular attention is given to the relationship between myocardial FAPI uptake, CMR tissue characterization, ventricular function, circulating biomarkers, and calculated arrhythmic risk. Although initial studies support the complementary value of FAPI PET and CMR for characterizing active and established myocardial remodelling, the available evidence remains limited by small, predominantly single-centre cohorts, heterogeneous radiotracers and acquisition protocols, and the absence of validated quantitative thresholds or prospective outcome data. Larger longitudinal studies are required to determine whether FAPI PET can provide incremental prognostic information or serve as a reproducible imaging biomarker for disease progression and therapeutic response.

title: Structural Optimization and Fatigue Performance Evaluation of Balloon-Expandable Aortic Valve Stents.
authors: Tao Cai; Chaoqun Zhao; Gang Fang
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a critical therapy for aortic stenosis, but most existing valve stents are designed for Western patients, whose aortic root anatomy differs from Chinese patients characterized by smaller annulus diameters, heavier calcification, and a higher prevalence of bicuspid valves. To address this mismatch, we designed a balloon-expandable aortic valve stent tailored for Chinese patients and systematically evaluated its performance. Four structural schemes were considered; a diamond-hexagonal composite mesh was selected based on radial strength, expansion uniformity, anchoring stability, sealing, and coronary access. Material properties of MP35N were obtained via tensile tests, and finite element models simulated crimping, recoil, and expansion. Among three end-corner geometries, the U-shaped design showed superior mechanical behavior with lower stress/strain concentrations. For stents crimped to 6.5 mm, maximum equivalent stress ranged from 1030 to 1076 MPa and plastic strain from 0.221 to 0.259; upon expansion to 20-29 mm, stress reached 1417-1493 MPa and strain 0.447-0.544, with strain concentrated at the corner ends. Simulated recoil matched experimental results within 7% relative error. Accelerated fatigue testing (4 × 108 cycles) of the bare stents revealed no fractures, displacements, or surface damage. These findings demonstrate that the optimized bare stent structure exhibits good mechanical feasibility, durability, and improved anatomical compatibility for Chinese TAVI patients, providing a promising device solution for domestic clinical application.

title: Kidney Function Trajectories in Patients with and Without Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Single-Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Hirofumi Sakuma; Satoshi Kawaguchi; Yuya Kitani; Tatsuya Aonuma; Naoko Kawabata; Erika Saito; Akiho Minoshima; Shingo Kunioka; Hiroyuki Kamiya; Naoki Nakagawa
abstract: Background/Objectives: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) may improve systemic hemodynamics and kidney perfusion; however, its effect on long-term kidney function remains unclear. We evaluated kidney function trajectories before and after TAVR in patients with and without chronic kidney disease (CKD). Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) who underwent TAVR between June 2016 and December 2024. Overall, 314 eligible patients were classified by baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) as without CKD (≥60 mL/min/1.73 m2) or with CKD (<60 mL/min/1.73 m2). Linear mixed-effects models estimated pre- and post-TAVR eGFR slopes, which were compared between groups after covariate adjustment. Results: Median follow-up was 2.0 years. Adjusted pre-TAVR eGFR slopes were -2.11 (95% confidence interval [CI], -3.34 to -0.89) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients without CKD and -2.83 (95% CI, -3.65 to -2.01) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients with CKD. The post-TAVR slopes were -4.02 (95% CI, -5.68 to -2.35) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients without CKD and -0.83 (95% CI, -2.04 to 0.39) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients with CKD, with a significant group difference of 3.19 (95% CI, 1.44 to 4.94) mL/min/1.73 m2/year (p < 0.001). In patients with CKD, the post-TAVR slope improved relative to the pre-TAVR slope by 2.01 (95% CI, 0.51 to 3.50) mL/min/1.73 m2/year (p < 0.01), whereas no significant change was observed in those without CKD. Conclusions: eGFR decline after TAVR was attenuated in patients with CKD compared with those without CKD, suggesting that kidney function may be preserved through hemodynamic improvement following TAVR.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Combined TAVR-PCI Versus SAVR-CABG in Patients with Aortic Stenosis and Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Ricardo Antonio Rodriguez Mejia; Mathhar Aldaoud; Ifeanyi Momodu; Merina Dongol; Girum Feyissa; Kelechi Aruogu; Zamaraq M Bhatti; Abdul Haseeb Riaz; Nafisa Saleem
abstract: Background/Objectives: Coronary artery disease coexists with severe aortic stenosis in about half of patients. Surgical aortic valve replacement with coronary artery bypass grafting (SAVR+CABG) is guideline-recommended, but transcatheter aortic valve replacement with percutaneous coronary intervention (TAVR+PCI) is increasingly used. Prior meta-analyses double-counted overlapping populations and did not report randomized evidence separately; we re-examined the comparison after correcting both. Methods: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Web of Science and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to July 2026 for randomized and comparative observational studies, excluding reports with overlapping populations. Outcomes were pooled with random-effects models, stratified by study design, and re-analysed without administrative databases. Certainty was rated with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Results: Fourteen studies were included (two randomized trials, nine cohorts, three administrative databases), comprising 154,892 patients (28,569 TAVR+PCI; 126,323 SAVR+CABG). TAVR+PCI was associated with lower early mortality (odds ratio (OR) 0.60, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.44-0.84) and less acute kidney injury (OR 0.34, 0.20-0.57), but greater pacemaker implantation (OR 2.18, 1.93-2.46) and major vascular complications (OR 3.38, 1.65-6.89). Stroke, myocardial infarction and one-year mortality (OR 0.80, 0.58-1.10) did not differ; bleeding results were inconsistent (I2 = 95%). Over 12-72 months, mortality was higher with TAVR+PCI (hazard ratio (HR) 1.38, 1.28-1.49; nine observational studies), unchanged without the largest cohort. Administrative databases drove heterogeneity but not the direction of any early outcome. Certainty was moderate for pacemaker implantation and low or very low otherwise; randomized data were too limited to confirm these findings. Conclusions: In predominantly observational evidence, TAVR+PCI was associated with lower early risk but higher mortality over longer follow-up. This trade-off supports individualized Heart Team decisions rather than the superiority of either strategy. Adequately powered randomized trials with long-term follow-up are needed.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Complex Anatomy: An Anatomy-Driven Framework for Bicuspid Stenosis, Pure Aortic Regurgitation, and the Small Annulus in the Era of Lifetime Management.
authors: Daniel Miron Brie; Cristian Mornoș; Roxana Popescu; Alina Diduța Brie
abstract: Background: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation is established for severe calcific tricuspid aortic stenosis, but its application in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) stenosis, pure native aortic regurgitation (AR), and small aortic annulus anatomy remains limited by heterogeneous morphology, device-specific constraints, and uncertain long-term outcomes. These settings require decisions that extend beyond immediate procedural success to encompass coronary access, reintervention, valve durability, and associated aortopathy. This review synthesizes current evidence and proposes an anatomy-driven framework integrating imaging, device selection, procedural planning, and lifetime management. Methods: A structured narrative review was conducted in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) criteria. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from 1 January 2010 to 31 March 2026 for studies addressing TAVI in BAV stenosis, pure native AR, and small aortic annulus anatomy. Randomized trials, meta-analyses, multicenter registries, pivotal device studies, and guideline or consensus documents were prioritized. After screening 2663 records and assessing 330 full-text reports, 101 records were retained for qualitative synthesis. Evidence was appraised by anatomical substrate, imaging phenotype, device strategy, procedural hazards, and implications for lifetime management. Results: In BAV stenosis, contemporary registry and prospective cohort data support high device success and acceptable early and mid-term outcomes in carefully selected patients; however, calcified raphe, bulky asymmetric leaflet or left ventricular outflow tract calcification, annular eccentricity, and concomitant aortopathy identify higher-risk phenotypes that often favor surgery. Randomized evidence in younger low-risk BAV patients remains limited and exploratory, with the NOTION-2 trial showing a numerically higher 3-year composite event rate after TAVI than surgical aortic valve replacement (20.4% vs. 7.8%; hazard ratio 2.9, 95% confidence interval 0.9-9.0) in the small bicuspid subgroup. In pure native AR, lack of annular calcification and frequent root dilatation impair anchoring of conventional transcatheter heart valves, increasing risks of migration, embolization, residual AR, and second-valve implantation. Dedicated leaflet-anchoring devices have improved outcomes: in ALIGN-AR, the JenaValve Trilogy system achieved procedural success above 95% in high-surgical-risk patients, although evidence remains single-arm and nonrandomized. In small annuli, the strongest comparative evidence comes from the SMART trial, in which supra-annular self-expanding valves were non-inferior to balloon-expandable valves for the 12-month clinical composite and reduced moderate/severe prosthesis-patient mismatch at 30 days (11.2% vs. 35.3%). Across all three phenotypes, electrocardiography-gated computed tomography is fundamental for defining anchoring, sizing, calcium distribution, root and coronary anatomy, anticipated coronary re-access, and the feasibility of redo-TAVI. Surgery remains particularly relevant when aortic repair, annular/root enlargement, or a more durable lifetime strategy is required. Conclusions: TAVI is feasible in selected patients with BAV stenosis, pure native AR, and small aortic annuli, but the evidentiary strength and optimal procedural strategy differ substantially across these anatomies. Treatment should be guided by an anatomy-driven, computed-tomography-based Heart Team assessment that integrates immediate procedural feasibility with age, surgical candidacy, aortopathy, prosthesis-patient mismatch risk, coronary access, durability, and future reintervention options. Surgery remains the more established strategy for many younger, operable patients with unfavorable BAV morphology or aortopathy, AR with root dilatation, or very small annuli amenable to enlargement. Dedicated randomized trials, standardized imaging criteria, and long-term durability data are needed to refine lifetime management in complex aortic valve anatomy.

title: The Cusp-Overlap Technique Versus the Standard Three-Cusp Technique for Self-Expanding Transcatheter Aortic Valves-A Single-Center Experience.
authors: Alexandru Ispas; Damien Brunet; Redouane Saady; Yacoub Habib; Catalin Pestrea; Laurent Drogoul
abstract: Background: Conduction disturbances and the subsequent need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPMI) remain a major limitation of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with self-expanding transcatheter heart valves (SE-THVs). The cusp-overlap technique (COT) has been proposed to optimize implantation depth and reduce PPMI rates compared to the standard three-cusp technique (3CT). Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included 113 consecutive patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR with the Medtronic CoreValve Evolut™ SE-THV(Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) between September 2020 and March 2023. Patients were treated using either COT (n = 49) or 3CT (n = 62). Baseline characteristics, procedural outcomes, and 30-day clinical events were compared before and after one-to-one propensity score matching. The primary endpoint was the incidence of PPMI at hospital discharge; the secondary endpoint was a composite of death, stroke, life-threatening or disabling bleeding, major vascular complications, and moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation at 30 days. A post hoc power calculation was performed given the low observed event rate. Results: Procedural success was achieved in 98.2% of patients. In the unmatched cohort, PPMI occurred in 6.1% (COT) vs. 9.7% (3CT) (p = 0.48). In the matched cohort (49 pairs), PPMI rates were 6.1% (COT) vs. 12.2% (3CT) (p = 0.48). With only 3 vs. 6 PPMI events in the matched cohort, the study had an estimated post hoc power of approximately 19% (two-sided α = 0.05) to detect the observed difference, so the negative primary result should be regarded as inconclusive rather than as evidence of equivalence between techniques. The secondary composite endpoint occurred less frequently in the COT group both before matching (14.3% vs. 32.3%; p = 0.049) and after matching (14.3% vs. 30.6%, p = 0.049). This composite difference was driven predominantly by the moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation (PVL) component (12.2% vs. 24.2% unmatched; 12.2% vs. 22.4% matched) rather than by death, stroke, or major vascular complications. Evolut device generation differed markedly by arm (COT patients received later-generation devices far more often than 3CT; p < 0.001), and is presented in the Methods/Results Sections as a key temporal confounder. COT was associated with a lower incidence of moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation, without prolonging procedural time. Conclusions: In this real-world single-center cohort, the cusp-overlap technique was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in PPMI after TAVR with the CoreValve Evolut™ SE-THV. COT was, however, associated with fewer paravalvular leaks and a lower rate of the secondary composite of adverse clinical events at 30 days.

title: Lipoprotein(a): Particle vs mass and prevalent cardiovascular disease in the cardiovascular risk in Young Finns study population.
authors: Olli Raitakari; Matias Knuuti; Anna Linko-Parvinen; Katja Pahkala; Suvi Rovio; Noora Kartiosuo; Sini Stenbacka; Irina Lisinen; Britt-Marie Loo; Terho Lehtimäki; Mika Kähönen; Claudia Lamina; Florian Kronenberg; Markus Juonala; Jorma S A Viikari; Juha Mykkänen
abstract:
Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] can be reported as mass (mg/dL) or particle concentration (nmol/L). Because Lp(a) acts at the particle level, molar concentration may better reflect biologically relevant exposure.
To compare molar- and mass-based Lp(a) in relation to cardiovascular outcomes, risk classification, LPA genetic variation, and apo(a) isoform phenotype in the Young Finns Study.
Molar Lp(a) was measured using a traceable Roche Tina-quant Gen.2 assay and mass using a nontraceable Thermo Fisher assay. Associations with cardiovascular outcomes and aortic valve stenosis were assessed by logistic regression in adults aged ≥40 years (N = 3898). Agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis and guideline-based risk reclassification. Associations with LPA genetic risk score and apo(a) isoform phenotype were assessed using Spearman correlation.
Both metrics showed similar associations across cardiovascular outcomes, with significant associations for coronary artery disease (CAD) and aortic valve stenosis. In fully adjusted CAD models, the odds ratio for the highest vs lowest quintile was 1.55 for molar and 1.67 for mass. Agreement between guideline-based risk categories was 95.6%. Molar assigned 2.9% of individuals to a higher risk category than mass, vs 1.5% in the opposite direction. The molar-to-mass ratio was associated with LPA score and apo(a) isoform size, with greater attenuation after adjustment for molar than mass.
Molar and mass showed comparable associations with cardiovascular outcomes. However, molar reporting aligned more closely with the genetic and structural determinants of Lp(a) and more often assigned individuals to higher guideline-based risk categories, supporting continued standardization toward particle-based reporting.

title: Anatomically ROI- and IOI-informed Hybrid U-Net model for Abdominal Object Segmentation in CT images.
authors: Yadavendra Nln; Y Akhtar; Y Tong; T Liu; C Wu; I Singh; D Kim; M Costin; O Fabula; S Cao; K Zhang; Z Xu; D A Torigian; J K Udupa
journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
abstract: Segmentation in medical imaging is a critical and challenging task, essential for improved disease diagnosis, staging, treatment planning, and response assessment. Over the years, various deep learning (DL) methods have been developed to enhance image segmentation. Among these, encoder-decoder methods, particularly the U-Net model and its variants, have proven effective in medical image segmentation. These methods incrementally address the limitations of artificial intelligence (AI) in recognizing high-level object concepts by integrating different-level features. We add natural intelligence (NI) into AI and leverage anatomical knowledge to further improve object segmentation accuracy. Our study introduces the hybrid U-Net (HUN) model that focuses on regions of interest (ROI) and intensities of interest (IOI) determined by NI, thus enhancing resource utilization efficiency and reducing irrelevant information. The HUN model balances local and global feature extraction, improving segmentation outcomes in 15 of 16 objects of interest in abdominal low-dose CT images compared to the U-Net. The novel concept of hybrid intelligence (HI), which combines NI with AI/DL techniques, is explored, showcasing its robustness and generalizability across various medical imaging applications. Our findings underscore the importance of incorporating NI into AI-driven medical imaging methods, paving the way for more effective and reliable solutions in medical image analysis and holding significant potential for improving patient care and clinical outcomes.

title: Open-source hardware platform for automated, non-invasive plant phenotyping through combined RGB and thermal imaging.
authors: Marcel Bentancor; Esteban Casaretto; Omar Borsani; Gastón Quero; Mercedes Muñoz
abstract: We present an open-source, modular plant phenotyping platform for non-invasive monitoring of small to medium-sized plants in growth chambers. The system integrates an RGB camera and a FLIR Lepton 3.5 thermal module on an automated two-axis Cartesian gantry capturing overhead images at 24 predefined positions. A key design feature is the use of Hall effect sensors with permanent magnets for discrete position referencing, providing robust, recalibration-free positioning without complex mechanical systems such as lead screws, belt-driven encoders, or step-counting alone. The platform uses 3D-printed components, a Raspberry Pi, stepper motors with rack-and-pinion transmission, and commonly available hardware store materials. Automated image acquisition scheduling increases temporal resolution and eliminates errors from prolonged manual measurements. Companion software enables homography-based projection of RGB segmentation masks onto thermal images and interactive exploration and quantitative analysis of thermographic data. As proof of concept, a multi-day water deficit experiment with soybean plants was conducted. RGB images were segmented using a U-Net deep learning model, and projected leaf area dynamics clearly discriminated between irrigated and drought-stressed plants. Thermal imaging revealed canopy temperature differences consistent with stomatal closure under water deficit.

title: CAVASS-DL: An Enhanced Computer-Assisted Visualization and Analysis Software System by Integrating Deep Learning Segmentation Models.
authors: L Xie; G J Grevera; Y Tong; C Wu; Z Liu; D A Torigian; J K Udupa
journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
abstract: Segmentation in medical images plays a crucial first step for the quantitative analysis of organs of interest and disease conditions that may affect them. In the 2000s, we released an open-source medical image processing and analysis software system called CAVASS (Computer-Assisted Visualization and Analysis Software System), whose lineage goes back to 1980 as the first software for medical image processing. CAVASS supports multiple types of medical images and numerous usage scenarios/use cases. To allow ready access to advanced deep learning models within the easy-to-use graphical user interface (GUI) of CAVASS to greatly facilitate ground truth segmentation generation and production mode image segmentation, we created an enhanced version of CAVASS, called CAVASS-DL, by integrating the Segment Anything Model (SAM) within our software, which can extract and fuse the features from images and interactive prompts to enhance the segmentation performance. Firstly, we modified the GUI to enable intuitive region-of-interest (ROI) prompting via bounding boxes. Secondly, we implemented and trained the SAM network using PyTorch platform. Lastly, we bundled the SAM network as a standalone executable interface for CAVASS. The illustrative and quantitative results on 20 dynamic MRI scans of neck and thorax demonstrate that our approach achieves high accuracy and efficiency for semi-automatic anatomy object segmentation via CAVASS-DL in a convenient manner.

title: The German National Cohort: Ophthalmic Assessment, Baseline Profile, and Potential for Artificial Intelligence-Based Eye Research.
authors: Camila Roa; Ansgar Beuse; Alexandra Schweig; Sarah Müller; Klaus Berger; Caroline Brandl; Titus Brinker; Anne Elbrecht; Robert Finger; Gerd Geerling; Karin Halina Greiser; Carsten Grohmann; Kathrin Günther; Iris Heid; André Karch; Thomas Keil; Jessica Krepel; Michael Leitzmann; Claudia Meinke-Franze; Annette Peters; Sabine Schipf; Matthias Schulze; Alexander K Schuster; Stefan N Willich; Martin A Leitritz; Marius Ueffing; Philipp Berens
abstract:
To describe the ophthalmic examination protocol within the German National Cohort (NAKO)/NAKO Gesundheitsstudie, to report the baseline profile of participants undergoing ophthalmic assessment, and to illustrate the potential as a population-based resource for artificial intelligence (AI) research in eye health.
Baseline analysis of ophthalmic data within the nationwide, population-based multicenter prospective NAKO study.
Forty-eight thousand four hundred and sixty adults in the ophthalmic level 2 module of 205 053 adults enrolled in NAKO, aged 19-74 years, with a mean age 48.9 ± 12.5 years, and 52.7% were male.
All participants underwent standardized biomedical examinations and detailed questionnaire-based data collection, including nondilated color fundus imaging, visual acuity testing, and a brief ocular history. Ocular health was summarized using descriptive statistics. Fundus image quality and morphological features (e.g., cup-to-disc ratio and arteriolar-to-venular ratio) were assessed using open-source deep learning models. Standard deep learning architectures were trained on the fundus images to predict age, sex, and blood pressure.
Percentage of fundus images graded as good quality; mean absolute error (MAE) for age and blood pressure prediction; accuracy for sex prediction.
The analysis includes 48 460 participants who completed the ophthalmic baseline examination of NAKO. Mean visual acuity (logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution) was 0.01 ± 0.20 (left eye, mean ± standard deviation) and 0.03 ± 0.21 (right eye). Self-reported ocular disease prevalence was 4.2% for cataract, 2.0% for glaucoma, and 0.9% for macular degeneration; 68.2% of fundus images were classified as gradable using 4 deep learning-based quality grading models. Morphological features showed systematic differences across age groups. Standard deep learning architectures showed comparative performance to the state-of-the-art for age, sex, and blood pressure prediction (2.96 MAE for age prediction, 0.84 accuracy for sex prediction, and 10.78 and 6.97 MAE for systolic and diastolic blood pressure prediction).
The German National Cohort provides a large-scale, nationwide population-based resource with visual acuity measurements and systemic health indicators, as well as color fundus images in about 50 000 NAKO participants. These data lay the groundwork for studying eye health in the general adult population in Germany and can serve as a strong foundation for developing and validating AI tools in eye health research.
Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

title: Sleep Stage Classification Across Heterogeneous EEG/EOG Channels with Multi-channel Differential Transformer.
authors: Benjamin Wei Hao Chin; Yuin Torng Yew; Jia Hong Puah; Haocheng Wu; Lanxin Liang; Chow Khuen Chan; Norita Mohd Zain; Siti Balqis Samdin; Sim Kuan Goh
abstract: Classification of sleep stages is essential for assessing sleep quality and diagnosing sleep disorders. However, manual inspection of EEG characteristics for each stage is time-consuming and prone to human error. Although machine learning and deep learning methods have been actively developed, they continue to face challenges arising from the non-stationarity and variability of electroencephalography (EEG) and electrooculography (EOG) signals across diverse clinical configurations, often resulting in poor generalization. In this work, we propose SleepDIFFormer, a multi-channel differential transformer framework for heterogeneous EEG-EOG representation learning. SleepDIFFormer is trained across multiple sleep staging datasets, each treated as a source domain, with the goal of generalizing to unseen target domains. Specifically, it employs a Multi-channel Differential Transformer Architecture (MDTA) designed to process raw EEG and EOG signals while incorporating cross-domain alignment. Our approach mitigates spatial and temporal attention noise and learns a domain-invariant EEG-EOG representation through feature distribution alignment across datasets, thereby enhancing generalization to new domains. Empirically, we evaluated SleepDIFFormer on five diverse sleep staging datasets under domain generalization settings and benchmarked it against existing approaches, achieving superior performance. Furthermore, comprehensive ablation analyses and interpretation of the differential attention weights demonstrated their relevance to learning discriminative sleep EEG representations. These findings support the development of more generalizable approaches to automated sleep-stage classification. Our source code and checkpoint are made publicly available at https://github.com/Ben1001409/SleepDIFFormer.

title: Hybrid foundation models: An investigation of foundation anatomy model and foundation segmentation model (FAM-FSM) on thoracic CT images for radiation therapy planning.
authors: Yubing Tong; Lipeng Xie; Dewey Odhner; Tiange Liu; Drew A Torigian; Jayaram K Udupa
journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
abstract: In this paper, we investigated a novel hybrid foundation model (HFM) by combining a foundation anatomy model and a foundation segmentation model (FAM-FSM) for automatic object segmentation on thoracic CT images for radiation therapy planning purposes. The HFM framework first performs object recognition and then object delineation for segmentation. The previous hybrid intelligence (HI) segmentation system using natural intelligence through anatomy models to provide recognition results as prompts to FSM enables the combination of existing recognition with the delineation from FSM. SAM-Med2D is adopted as the FSM for segmentation in this study. 249 thoracic CT images are utilized, and 7 objects of interest are assessed in the experiments. 125 data sets from one site are used for fine-tuning FSM, and 104 testing data sets from another 4 different clinical centers are used for testing the performance of segmentation. Different from the typical training strategy used in multi-center deep learning approaches and federated learning, we did not mix data sets from different centers for training purposes in our study. Instead, consistent and strict body region and object definitions as foundational knowledge and guidance were shared and followed by each clinical center in training and testing. HFM achieved promising results from 4 different centers compared to results from FSM using manual ROI prompts. We also show that the existing FSM might not perform well on challenging objects compared to small but specific trained models. The proposed HFM framework can easily integrate any other prompt-based FSMs.

title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
authors: Jian Ding; Yuhan Chen; Feifan Liu; Jun Han; Xiang Zhu; Yangyang Li; Tianyu Lu; Sheng Hu; Jingjing Fu; Shiying Gai; Huan Liu; Song Cheng; Dekuai Tong; Yougen Cheng
abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

title: MTL-LymphNet: A Lightweight Multi-Task Learning Framework for Simultaneous Lymph Node Segmentation and Metastasis Classification in Thyroid Cancer Ultrasound.
authors: Muhammad Thahiruddin; Imam Wahyudi; Alfie Nuril Mustofa
abstract: Ultrasound assessment of cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma is crucial but suffers from inter-observer variability. Existing deep learning solutions typically use separate single-task pipelines, resulting in parameter redundancy. We propose MTL-LymphNet, a lightweight, backbone-agnostic multi-task learning framework that simultaneously segments lymph nodes and classifies metastasis within a single forward pass, evaluated across 3 backbones and 4 loss weighting strategies. On 338 images from 2 independent clinical centers, MTL-LymphNet achieved an internal cross-validation Dice coefficient of 0.891 ± 0.022 and AUC of 0.948 ± 0.027. Bidirectional external validation revealed substantial domain shift, with cross-center Dice of 0.865 and 0.779, and AUC of 0.733 and 0.830. The multi-task configuration offered a favorable efficiency-performance trade-off (∆Dice = Δ, -0.014, P < .0001) for 40% fewer parameters than separate models. No backbone or weighting strategy consistently dominated, and calibration degraded substantially under domain shift (ECE: 0.049 internally vs 0.178-0.304 externally), requiring center-specific recalibration before clinical use. To our knowledge, this is the first MTL framework for cervical lymph node analysis with bidirectional multi-center validation and systematic ablation. With a compact size of 22.6 to 29.1 MB and CPU inference of 81 to 131 ms, MTL-LymphNet demonstrates technical feasibility as a CAD tool warranting prospective validation.

title: Evaluating different large language model performances in evidence-based dental implantology: a blinded controlled experimental evaluation using expert panel assessment.
authors: Vasilios Alevizakos; Robert Gaudin; Iman Ghanad; Jonathan von See; Theodor von See; Florin Eggmann; Constantin von See
abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for clinical decision-making and evidence-based information retrieval in dental implantology. However, concerns remain regarding the accuracy, reliability, and clinical applicability of different AI approaches, including general-purpose, fine-tuned, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models. This study aimed to compare their ability to provide accurate, evidence-based, and clinically relevant responses to implantology-related questions.
Sixteen master's-level clinical questions were presented to all four LLMs under controlled conditions. Their anonymized responses were independently evaluated by three dental implantology specialists based on three core criteria: specificity, accuracy, and clinical utility, using a 0-10 scale. Descriptive statistics were reported as medians and interquartile ranges. Differences among models were assessed primarily using Kruskal-Wallis tests, and inter-rater reliability was evaluated using Fleiss' kappa.
LLM4 consistently achieved the highest median scores across all criteria (Specificity: median 9.0, IQR 9.0-10.0; Accuracy: median 9.5, IQR 9.0-10.0; Clinical Utility: median 10.0, IQR 9.0-10.0), significantly outperforming the other models (all p < 0.001). Cohen's d revealed large to very large effect sizes in comparisons involving LLM4, particularly against LLM2 and LLM3. LLM2 scored lowest and showed the highest variability. Inter-rater reliability was slight across all metrics (κ = 0.078-0.180), indicating moderate evaluator disagreement.
Among the models tested, LLaMA 3.2 + RAG demonstrated superior and more consistent clinical performance in dental implantology. While fine-tuning provided moderate benefits, real-time access to structured guidelines significantly enhanced response quality. Despite low inter-rater agreement, these findings highlight the promise of RAG models in supporting high-complexity, evidence-based clinical domains, while emphasizing the need for standardization in AI evaluation protocols.

title: Concordance between large language models and orthodontists in photo-based orthodontic assessment.
authors: Feridun Abay
abstract:
The widespread use of digital platforms for preliminary health information has increased interest in artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools in dentistry. Large language model (LLM)-based systems are increasingly used for patient education and preliminary clinical guidance. However, their clinical consistency in orthodontic assessments based solely on intraoral photographs remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical appropriateness of LLM-generated orthodontic assessments compared with blinded expert orthodontist evaluations.
This blinded comparative agreement study included 104 patients aged ≥ 12 years undergoing orthodontic evaluation. For each case, three standardized intraoral photographs and basic demographic data were submitted to two LLM-based systems (ChatGPT-4o and Grok 4.1) using a standardized prompt. Responses to five clinical questions were independently evaluated by three expert orthodontists using a 5-point Likert scale. Consensus scores were obtained by averaging the ratings of the three evaluators. Inter-system comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) corrections were applied for multiple comparisons.
Mean ratings were generally ≥ 3, indicating moderate clinical acceptability. After correction for multiple comparisons, the most robust finding was the significantly higher rating assigned to ChatGPT-4o for the recommended orthodontic treatment approach in Dental Class I patients. In the 12-15-year subgroup, ChatGPT-4o also received higher ratings for treatment recommendation; however, statistical significance was retained only after FDR correction and not after Bonferroni adjustment. No significant differences were observed across most other evaluated parameters, particularly malocclusion classification. In patients older than 15 years, paired differences between the two systems were highly similar, resulting in an insufficient number of non-zero differences for reliable Wilcoxon signed-rank testing.
LLM-based systems may provide clinically acceptable outputs in selected orthodontic assessment domains when evaluations are based solely on intraoral photographs. However, variability persists in complex decision-making tasks, particularly treatment planning. Current evidence supports the use of such systems as supportive tools operating under professional supervision rather than as independent clinical decision-makers.

title: Impact of a silver filter with deep learning reconstruction on non-contrast MDCT of adrenal glands in terms of image quality, density values and radiation dose.
authors: Catherine Roy; Quentin le Duff; Luc Mertz; Hugo Jaillet; Aissam Labani; Sébastien Moliére; Mickael Ohana
abstract:
To investigate whether the use of a silver beam filtration with deep learning reconstruction (DLR) impact the normal adrenal gland on unenhanced MDCT in terms of density, image quality and radiation dose.
This unicentric retrospective study evaluated two unenhanced MDCT acquisitions of 123 patients performed with a conventional filtration (Group A) and with a silver filtration (Group B) on a 320-detector row CT scanner with DLR. A total of 246 series, corresponding to 492 adrenal glands, were analyzed. We recorded the HU values of the normal adrenal gland, subcutaneous fat and extra corporeal air as well as the radiation dose and assessed image quality.
The subjective image quality was excellent, with no significant difference between the two acquisitions with a mean score on the Likert scale of 4.6 ± 0.3 and 4.1 ± 0.6 for groups A and B, respectively (p = 0.09). Interobserver agreement for image quality was good and quite similar for both groups (group B: k= 0.86; group A: k= 0.90). The mean density of adrenal gland was 15.65 ± 5.5 HU with conventional filtration (Group A) and 13.05 ± 4.5 HU for silver filtration (Group B). For the right adrenal gland, the median values were 15.8 HU and 12.9 HU for group A and B, respectively (p=0.01). For the left adrenal gland, the median values were 15.5 HU and 13.2 HU for group A and B, respectively (p=0.03). A subgroup of 135 adrenal glands (including both right and left side) with a density value ≤ 15HU using conventional filtration (Subgroup A) showed a statistically significant lower median value with silver filtration (Subgroup B). Inside this ≤ 15 HU subgroup, 59 adrenal glands had a density value equal or lower than 10 HU of which 48 belonged to subgroup B. A reduction in HU values of 18% was observed with the silver filter in the overall cohort (492 adrenal glands), and 26% in the subgroup ≤ 15 HU. Similarly, the mean score for image noise was 7.6 ± 1.5 for conventional filter and 8.3 ± 0.9 for silver filtration, with no statistically significant difference (p = 0.08). Radiation dose was significantly reduced by 35% in examinations performed with silver filtration when compared to conventional filter.
The spontaneous density of normal adrenal gland is lower than previously reported. Implementing silver filtration with DLR in CT acquisition achieves a significant radiation dose reduction while preserving image quality, along with a decrease in adrenal gland HU values, often below 10 HU. This must be taken into account as this is the threshold of the key reference for adenoma.
This study is part of a routine clinical practice. This unicentric retrospective study was approved by our local institutional review board, and written informed patient consent was not required. The patients were orally informed that their second CT examination will be performed using the newest technology available on the CT machine in our department.

title: Deep Learning and Engineered Biomaterials-Enhanced Imaging-Guided Cancer Immunotherapy.
authors: Kaiwei Lv; Bin Li; Bing Xiao; Fei Zhou; Hui Zhao; Jihong Sun; Jun-Long Liang
abstract: The clinical success of immunotherapies is hindered by the absence of robust methodologies for the early and accurate assessment of antitumor immune responses. Integrating engineered biomaterials with artificial intelligence (AI)-driven molecular imaging technology offers a powerful approach for predicting immune efficacy. However, its clinical translation is significantly hindered by several critical limitations, including the complex and costly synthesis of multifunctional imaging probes, insufficient deep-tissue penetration, suboptimal in vivo signal-to-noise ratios, potential immunogenicity and off-target toxicity, and the limited generalizability of deep learning models across heterogeneous patient populations. In view of these pressing scientific challenges, this review focuses on the application of chemical and biomolecular strategies-enhanced engineered biomaterials in promoting the sensitivity and specificity of advanced imaging modalities for visualizing signaling molecules and immune cells in the tumor microenvironment (TME). Meanwhile, recent progress in deep learning-driven image analysis has enabled strong predictive capabilities and automated the understanding of complex immune system dynamics. Together, these technologies provide a transformative platform for non-invasive monitoring, personalized treatment, and response prediction, with the potential to advance precision immuno-oncology and significantly impact both basic research and clinical translation.

title: Accuracy of transfer learning in predicting peri-implantitis onset from intraoral radiograph: A multi-center longitudinal retrospective study.
authors: Muhammad H A Saleh; Luigi Nibali; Abdusalam E Alrmali; Vito Carlo Alberto Caponio; Pasquale Santamaria; Francesco Fanelli; Khrystyna Zhurakivska; Hom-Lay Wang; Giuseppe Troiano
abstract:
The growing application of artificial intelligence in dentistry has opened new opportunities for predicting peri-implantitis (PI) using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Transfer learning, where knowledge from a model pre-trained on a large dataset is adapted to a new, domain-specific task, may enhance performance, particularly when medical datasets are limited. This study evaluated the ability of several pre-trained CNN architectures applied to baseline 2D intraoral radiographs to predict peri-implantitis onset.
A retrospective multi-center study was conducted at the University of Michigan and King's College London. A total of 195 implants (146 from Michigan and 49 from London) placed in 108 maintained patients were included. For each implant, a baseline periapical radiograph taken up to one year after prosthetic restoration was analyzed. Five pre-trained CNN architectures (ResNet50, DenseNet, VGG16, InceptionV3, EfficientNet) were combined with four transfer learning strategies: feature extraction (hybrid and non-hybrid), partial fine-tuning (50% of layers), and full fine-tuning. Models were trained using patient-wise splits to avoid leakage, and performance was evaluated on an independent test set using accuracy, area under the ROC curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity.
All CNN architectures showed variable performance across transfer learning strategies. The non-hybrid feature extraction approach provided the most consistent discrimination, with the best models achieving AUC values between 0.74 and 0.83. InceptionV3 reached the highest AUC (0.83). Fine-tuning strategies yielded modest or low performance, with AUCs generally ranging from 0.42 to 0.69 across architectures.
Non-hybrid feature extraction applied to pre-trained CNNs showed the most promising, though moderate, performance for predicting PI onset from baseline intraoral radiographs. These findings indicate that transfer learning may assist early risk stratification in implant dentistry, but larger prospective studies are needed before clinical adoption.
Deep learning models may serve as adjunctive tools to identify implants at higher risk for future PI based on routine baseline radiographs, supporting more individualized maintenance protocols and earlier preventive interventions.

title: Deep learning coupled with scalable domain-specific structural validation expands RNA virus discovery from metatranscriptomes.
authors: Gaoyang Luo; Zelin Zang; Ling Yuan; Jingbo Zhou; Ao Dong; Yufei Huang; Stan Z Li; Feng Ju
abstract: The discovery of RNA viruses from metatranscriptomic data remains challenging due to extreme sequence divergence and length heterogeneity, ranging from massive polyproteins to short assembly artifacts. We present Rider, a two-stage framework that synergizes deep representation learning with scalable domain-specific structural validation. In the first stage, Rider leverages a compact pretrained protein language model to broadly detect highly divergent viral signals. To overcome the inherent input length limitations of language models and accurately capture catalytic core domains, the second stage employs an overlapping sliding-window structure prediction strategy. These structures are then aligned against our curated database of non-redundant RdRp (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) domains. This domain-centric design detects RdRp domains embedded within long polyproteins and truncated fragments. Across >10,000 metatranscriptomes spanning diverse ecosystems, Rider achieves sensitivity comparable to LucaProt, recalling >99% of previously cataloged RNA viruses. Rider identifies thousands of deeply divergent sequences and clades that elude existing methods. In a human inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) cohort, Rider agrees with other methods in detecting RNA viruses while extending detection to divergent lineages, providing a scalable pipeline for global RNA virome exploration.

title: Automated screening of autism via a pretrained vision-language model in naturalistic caregiver-child interactions.
authors: Ruikang Deng; Huishi Huang; Shaoli Lv; Yu Xing; Yijie Li; Cong You; Fei Wu; Hongzhu Deng; Zhengxing Huang
abstract: Early autism screening is essential for timely intervention but remains constrained by specialist dependence, costly protocols, and limited accessibility. We present Autism-CLIP, a vision-language model that automates screening from 3-min naturalistic caregiver-child interaction videos recorded in toddlers aged 15-24 months. By integrating contrastive learning, large language model-generated supervision, domain-specific architecture, and hybrid training, Autism-CLIP aligns visual behavioral cues with autism-related assessment outcomes, enabling annotation-free inference. In multicenter evaluation, Autism-CLIP achieved an AUC of 0.903 in the internal cohort (n = 103) and 0.873 in the external cohort (n = 102), outperforming conventional machine learning methods. Attention mapping highlighted clinically relevant markers, including gaze aversion and limited social reciprocity. Requiring only smartphone-captured videos without manual coding or controlled settings, Autism-CLIP offers a scalable, low-cost approach to broaden access to early autism screening and support prioritization of clinical resources.

title: [Impact of Hybrid Iterative Reconstruction Combined with a Sharpening Filter on Coronary Artery Stent Profile Characteristics and Visual Assessment in Coronary CT Angiography: A Phantom Study].
authors: Mizuki Kakisako; Ryo Watanabe; Makoto Fujiwara; Kenta Maruyama
abstract:
In coronary CT angiography, we compared the profile characteristics and visual assessment of coronary stents between hybrid iterative reconstruction combined with a sharpening filter (S-HIR) and deep learning reconstruction (DLR).
We scanned a performance evaluation phantom and a custom-made phantom incorporating a coronary artery stent with an inner diameter of 3.5 mm. Images were reconstructed using DLR, hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR), and S-HIR of three sharpening strengths. We evaluated task-based transfer function (TTF) values, the maximum CT number of the stent struts, the error rate of the stent lumen diameter, rectangularity, and visual assessment performed by nine radiological technologists using Scheffé's paired comparison method.
In S-HIR, TTF values and rectangularity increased, while the error rate decreased with increasing sharpening strength. Visual assessment revealed no significant difference between sharpening medium filter+HIR (SM-HIR) and DLR. In contrast, sharpening high filter+HIR (SH-HIR) resulted in an excessive increase in the maximum CT number of the stent struts, and visual assessment scores decreased.
The S-HIR method newly proposed in this study altered the profile characteristics of coronary artery stents and improved their visibility in coronary CT angiography under phantom conditions. In particular, SM-HIR showed no statistically significant difference from DLR in visual assessment and could serve as a useful technique for improving coronary stent visibility in CT systems without DLR.

title: Adaptive local region super-resolution for high-field MRI: A diffusion-based approach with structural and frequency-domain constraints.
authors: Jianwei Zuo; Huifang Yang; Yumeng Tang; Xiaoyan Wang; Kai Zhong; Xin Peng; Jiajia Luo
abstract: High-field MRI offers superior SNR but is constrained by the trade-off between spatial resolution and acquisition time. Existing global deep learning super-resolution (SR) methods often incur computational overhead by ignoring regional image content. This motivates an adaptive local SR strategy to optimize efficiency and detail preservation. To address this, we developed a local SR method that adaptively allocates computational resources to information-rich regions. The proposed framework regularized an entropy-based local region processing strategy with a diffusion model fortified by frequency-domain and structural constraints. We retrospectively evaluated our method on two diverse datasets: a proprietary 7.0 T dental MRI dataset (25 T2-weighted DESS sequences from 10 beagle dogs) and a public 5.0 T brain MRI dataset (Diff5T, 50 diffusion-weighted sequences). Image quality was quantified using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID. On the 7.0 T dental test dataset (2 subjects), our method achieved a PSNR of 27.31 [26.83, 27.79] dB and the lowest LPIPS of 0.19 [0.18, 0.20]. On the 5.0 T brain test dataset (10 subjects), the method achieved a PSNR of 27.15 ± 0.10 dB, an LPIPS of 0.14 ± 0.00 and an FID of 54.01, with lower perceptual metrics than the evaluated baselines.
