Ablation studies indicated that the proposed frequency-domain and structural constraints reduced LPIPS and FID, with trade-offs in PSNR and SSIM. In conclusion, the evaluated framework showed improvements in perceptual metrics by integrating targeted local processing with frequency-domain and structural regularization, accompanied by a trade-off in pixel-wise fidelity metrics, supporting the technical feasibility of addressing the resolution-time trade-off in high-field MRI. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and evaluating the framework in human dental cohorts to address anatomical differences between the current canine model and human dental anatomy.

title: Integrating graph attention networks and deep learning with multi-stage computational screening: Bisdemethoxycurcumin as a potent A₂A receptor inhibitor for Parkinson's disease.
authors: Khaled Otmanine; Mounir Hammoudi; Houari Bendriss; Brahim Feraoun; Selma Mekhane; Nesrine Gherioune; Cherrouk Benmehache; Ichraf Kerrouzi; Khadidja Ayadi; Khaled El Miloudi; Meryem Amal Benghalia; Mustapha Kamel Otmanine; Mohamed Hentabli
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) remains a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with limited disease modifying therapies, as current treatments such as L-DOPA offer only symptomatic relief and are associated with severe adverse effects. This study presents an integrated multi-stage computational pipeline that combines quantitative structure activity relationship (QSAR) modelling enhanced by graph attention networks (GATs), molecular docking, density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and ADMET profiling to identify natural inhibitors targeting four key PD related proteins: adenosine A₂A receptor (A₂AR), gamma aminobutyric acid type A receptor (GABA-A), nuclear factor erythroid 2- related factor 2 (Nrf2), and (α-synuclein). A comprehensive dataset of 1393 structurally diverse compounds derived from 6- hydroxybenzothiazole 2-carboxamide and related scaffolds was assembled and used to train and validate seven regression algorithms. GATs achieved superior predictive performance (R2 = 0.991, Q2 = 0.987, RMSE = 0.487), outperforming Extra Trees (R2 = 0.742), Random Forest (R2 = 0.761), and SVR-RBF (R2 = 0.65). The large dataset size enhanced model generalizability, reduced overfitting risk, and enabled robust feature selection from an expanded descriptor pool of 312 molecular descriptors. Y-randomization with 100 permutations confirmed that all models with meaningful predictive performance were free from chance correlation (ΔQ2 > 0.50), validating the robustness of the QSAR workflow. Molecular docking of six phytochemicals derived from Curcuma longa (ar-turmerone, α -turmerone, bisdemethoxycurcumin) and Salvia officinalis (camphor, 1,8-cineole, α, β-thujone) revealed that bisdemethoxycurcumin BDMC exhibited the strongest binding affinity to the A₂A receptor (-9.1 kcal/mol) among the evaluated phytochemicals. L-DOPA, the current clinical standard of care, displayed weak affinity to the A₂A receptor (-7.2 kcal/mol), consistent with its known mechanism as a dopamine precursor rather than an A₂A ligand. DFT calculations at the B3LYP/6311G(d,p) level showed that BDMC possessed the lowest HOMO- LUMO energy gap (0.1428 eV) and the highest electrophilicity index (ω = 0.1477), indicating superior chemical reactivity and electron accepting capacity. A 200 ns MD simulation confirmed stable BDMC A₂A receptor binding, with 3-8 (mean ≈ 5) persistent hydrogen bonds and no dissociation events throughout the trajectory, as evidenced by centre of mass distance analysis and principal component analysis. ADMET profiling using SwissADME and ProTox II classified BDMC as blood brain barrier (BBB) permeable, compliant with Lipinski's Rule of Five, and safe (LD₅₀ = 2560 mg/kg, toxicity Class 5), compared to L-DOPA (Class 4, LD₅₀ = 1460 mg/kg). Comparative analysis demonstrated that BDMC offers superior predicted binding affinity to the A₂A receptor and a more favourable predicted toxicity profile compared to L-DOPA, positioning it as a compelling A₂A receptor-targeting lead candidate for PD therapy. Collectively, these findings establish a robust computational framework for accelerating drug discovery in neurodegenerative diseases and highlight BDMC as a promising A₂A Receptor inhibitor warranting further in-vitro and in- vivo experimental validation.

title: Feature selection and dimensionality reduction in multi-omics.
authors: Sweta Rai; Igor Kovalchuk
abstract: High-throughput multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional, heterogeneous and noisy datasets, making robust biomarker discovery and disease modelling challenging. This review critically examines dimensionality reduction and representation strategies for multi-omics analysis while distinguishing three related but different goals: feature selection, feature extraction/representation learning, and multi-omics integration. We use sparse canonical correlation analysis (sCCA), variational autoencoders (VAEs), and graph convolutional networks (GCNs) as representative case studies spanning sparse linear, probabilistic deep-learning, and graph-based approaches. Rather than treating these methods as interchangeable, we compare their data requirements, assumptions, interpretability, ability to accommodate non-linearity and missing modalities, computational demands, and validation needs. Applications across cancer, cardiovascular and neurodegenerative disease, and across bulk, single-cell, spatial and imaging multi-omics are summarized in comparative tables. We conclude with practical guidance for matching method families to biological questions and emphasize that robust biomarker claims require leakage-free model development, stability assessment and independent validation.

title: AI-bioinformatics synergy for precision medicine in brain diseases: integrating radiomics and multi-omics data.
authors: Bekir Altas; Polymnia Georgiou; Anna Onisiforou
abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and bioinformatics is reshaping the landscape of precision medicine in brain diseases, particularly in neurological diseases and brain tumors. Despite advances in both fields, the combined application of radiomics and multi-omics fusion remains underutilized, even though integrative frameworks are essential for addressing the complexity and heterogeneity of imaging and molecular data. This review examines how integrative AI-bioinformatics frameworks enable the fusion of radiomics with genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and other omics modalities to more comprehensively model disease complexity. Leveraging deep learning, graph neural networks, and advanced representation learning, these multimodal systems facilitate biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and personalized treatment strategies. We critically evaluate key challenges including data heterogeneity, limited interpretability, and barriers to clinical validation, and highlight emerging solutions aimed at enhancing reproducibility and translational readiness. Case studies in gliomas, Alzheimer's disease, and multiple sclerosis illustrate the clinical utility of unified imaging-omics architectures. Ultimately, this review positions radiomics and multi-omics integration as a foundational approach for the next generation of precision medicine in brain diseases by bridging the gap between computational innovation and clinical application.

abstract: Introduction: Height, weight, and age of person has significant impact on the normal size of heart. title: Prognostic value of the ECG strain pattern in aortic stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Yara El Deghel; Tony John Azizi
abstract: Review title: Prognostic value of the ECG strain pattern in aortic stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis Type and method of review: Meta analysis Stage of review at time of this submission: Review ongoing — the protocol has been finalised and the peer-reviewed search prepared; formal screening not yet started. Review question: In Adults with aortic stenosis, what is the effect of ECG left ventricular strain pattern compared with No ECG strain pattern on All-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (including aortic valve replacement)? Searches: The following sources will be searched: Europe PMC (PubMed, MEDLINE & preprints), PubMed / MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection. Additional records may be imported from other databases. No date or language restrictions are applied unless otherwise stated. The search strategy underwent peer review (PRESS) before execution. Condition or domain being studied: Adults with aortic stenosis Participants / population: Adults with aortic stenosis Intervention(s), exposure(s): ECG left ventricular strain pattern Comparator(s) / control: No ECG strain pattern Types of study to be included: Inclusion criteria: Adults with aortic stenosis; ECG strain pattern defined; Reports hazard ratios or event data for mortality or MACE; Prospective or retrospective cohort studies; Full-text article published in English. Exclusion criteria: No outcome follow-up; Strain assessed only by echocardiography (speckle-tracking); Reviews, editorials, letters or conference abstracts; Overlapping cohorts (the largest or most recent report is kept) Main outcome(s): All-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (including aortic valve replacement) Data extraction (selection and coding): Two reviewers will independently screen titles/abstracts and full texts, blinded to each other’s decisions, and extract data in duplicate using a standardised, piloted form. Disagreements will be resolved by discussion or a third reviewer. Risk of bias (quality) assessment: The risk of bias of each included study will be assessed independently by two reviewers using a study-design-appropriate tool. Disagreements will be resolved by consensus. Risk of bias in the review itself will be appraised with ROBIS. Strategy for data synthesis: Results will be synthesised narratively. Where studies are sufficiently homogeneous, effect estimates will be pooled in a meta-analysis using a fixed- or random-effects model as indicated by heterogeneity (I²). The certainty of the evidence will be rated using GRADE.

title: Low-Dose Glucocorticoids Adjunctive to Flow Diverter Therapy for Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms Improve Cerebrovascular Outcomes
authors: Zhuohua Wen; Xiheng Chen; Xin Tong; Chi Huang; Mengshi Huang; Jiancheng Lin; Anqi Xu; Hanyan Yang; Xiru Zhang; Yuanqi Lin; Jiwan Huang; Runze Ge; Hao Yuan; Chao Peng; Yanchao Liu; Fa Jin; 苏世星; Xin Zhang; Xifeng Li; Zongduo Guo; Ming Lv; Aihua Liu; Chuan‐Zhi Duan; Xin Feng
abstract: Abstract Flow diverter (FD) implantation is standard for unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs), but cerebrovascular complications persist. This nested study within a prospective multicenter cohort evaluates whether short-term, low-dose glucocorticoid use is associated with cerebrovascular outcomes after FD implantation. Propensity-score matching with exact matching on UIA location yielded 1327 patients (360 glucocorticoid-treated; 967 controls). Intravenous glucocorticoids, initiated within 2 hours of the FD procedure and administered for ≥2 days, were associated with fewer in-hospital cerebrovascular events (6.9% vs. 13.1%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.53) and major cerebrovascular events (4.7% vs. 12.4%; aOR, 0.37). Over a median 2-year follow-up, glucocorticoid use was also associated with fewer new-onset major cerebrovascular events (3.6% vs. 8.7%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.41) and less in-stent stenosis (7.9% vs. 13.2%; aOR, 0.55). Findings remained robust in unmatched patients on sensitivity analyses. We demonstrate that perioperative glucocorticoid regimens may reduce cerebrovascular events and in-stent stenosis in FD-treated patients, warranting randomized trials.

title: Multistage Preclinical Evaluation of MRI-Guided Stenting for Coarctation of the Aorta using in vitro and Porcine Models
authors: Denis Gholami Bajestani; C. Martin Reich; Jan Birkigt; Christina Mulik; Johannes Kauffold; Haukur Sigmarsson; Thies Jochimsen; Bernhard Sattler; Osama Sabri; Michael Steinmetz; Andreas Melzer
abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the technical and procedural feasibility of MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA using a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A commercially available MR Conditional guidewire and dedicated research prototypes comprising nitinol stents, delivery systems, and balloon catheters were assessed in a three-stage protocol. Device visibility was evaluated in a standardized water phantom at 1.5 T and 3.0 T. In a polymer-based CoA vessel phantom, 10 stent implantations were performed by novices (n = 6) and experts (n = 4), with four separate expert-led balloon dilatations. MRI-guided stent implantation was subsequently performed in five porcine models. RESULTS: All devices were visible at both field strengths, with lateral artifact widths of 5.3-7.8 mm for the guidewire, 20.9-38.5 mm for the stent delivery system, 13.1-19.9 mm for the expanded stents, and 17.4-30.5 mm for the balloon catheter. Phantom stenting duration was 10.2 ± 7.2 mins for novices and 6.2 ± 2.7 mins for experts. MRI-guided stent implantation was successfully performed in all five animals, with a mean duration of 13.6 ± 7.5 mins. In one animal, balloon post-dilatation was additionally performed as a procedural proof of concept. CONCLUSION: MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA is feasible within a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol and supports further clinical translation of radiation-free endovascular treatment.

title: Severe Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis With Multivalvular Abnormalities in a British-Born Adult Without a Recognized History of Acute Rheumatic Fever
authors: Adel Kenawi; Hatem Ali Abdelnasser; Nouralhuda Hamad; Marwa Ruziek; Ahmed Jaber
abstract: Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) has become uncommon in the United Kingdom, particularly among Britishborn adults without a recognized history of acute rheumatic fever (ARF).A 40-year-old British-born female with no previously diagnosed cardiac disease presented with a one-year history of progressive exertional dyspnoea.Chest radiography demonstrated cardiomegaly, and the N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide concentration was 1,800 pg/mL.Transthoracic echocardiography showed very severe mitral stenosis with characteristic rheumatic morphology, a mitral valve area of 0.33 cm² by planimetry, and a mean transmitral gradient of 16.6 mmHg.Associated findings included mild mitral regurgitation, tricuspid valve abnormalities with moderate-tosevere tricuspid regurgitation, and discordant aortic valve findings consistent with a low-flow, low-gradient pattern of aortic stenosis, an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of approximately 105-110 mmHg, left ventricular systolic impairment, and impaired right ventricular longitudinal systolic function.Further history identified intermittent involuntary left-hand movements, arthralgia, and an annular abdominal eruption with central pallor.These features raised the possibility of previously unrecognized rheumatic manifestations but were insufficient to establish the diagnosis of ARF.Following transoesophageal echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and multidisciplinary review, the patient underwent mitral and aortic valve replacement with tricuspid valve repair.This case highlights that advanced RHD can present without a documented history of ARF and emphasizes the importance of valve morphology, integrated haemodynamic assessment, and timely multidisciplinary management.

title: https://impactfactor.org/PDF/IJDDT/16/IJDDT,Vol16,Issue88s,Article36.pdf
authors: Saurav Gupta; Shaurya Bhatnagar; Sharanya Ray; Priyadarshini S. Nayak; S S Rajput
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Rheumatic mitral stenosis (MS) carries a substantial burden of morbidity in developing countries, and its progression is driven by fibrosis of the valve apparatus and the left atrium. No current medical therapy targets this fibrotic process. Dapagliflozin, a sodium–glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor established across the heart failure spectrum, has demonstrated anti-fibrotic actions in experimental settings and favorable effects on left atrial (LA) function in clinical studies. Objective: To evaluate whether dapagliflozin alters circulating fibrosis biomarkers (TGF-β1, PICP, MMP1, TIMP-1), LA function and NT-proBNP in rheumatic MS, and whether biomarker changes correlate with functional changes. Methods: In an open-label, randomized controlled trial (July–December 2025), 33 adults with rheumatic MS (mitral valve area ≤ 1.5 cm², NYHA class II–III) received either dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily plus standard treatment (n = 17) or standard treatment alone (n = 16) for four weeks. TGF-β1, PICP, MMP-1, TIMP-1 and NT-proBNP were quantified by ELISA, and LA function was derived echocardiographically as net atrioventricular compliance (Cn) and mitral mean pressure gradient (MPG), at baseline and follow-up. Between-group comparisons of pre–post changes were analyzed; p < 0.05 was considered significant. Results: Groups were well matched at baseline. After four weeks, PICP and TGF-β1 had risen from baseline in both arms, while the MMP-1/TIMP-1 ratio fell (significant within the dapagliflozin arm, p = 0.005); between-group differences in the magnitude of these changes were not significant for any biomarker. NTproBNP decreased more in the dapagliflozin group than in the control group, with a significant betweengroup difference in change (p = 0.034), although follow-up values did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.449). Dapagliflozin significantly improved LA function - higher Cn and lower MPG - relative to control. Changes in fibrosis biomarkers correlated neither with changes in Cn nor with changes in NTproBNP. Conclusion: Four weeks of dapagliflozin improved LA function and NT-proBNP in rheumatic MS without a detectable between-group effect on circulating fibrosis biomarkers. Larger and longer trials using tissuelevel imaging are needed to establish whether dapagliflozin modifies disease progression. Keywords: dapagliflozin; SGLT2 inhibitor; rheumatic heart disease; mitral stenosis; atrial fibrosis; TGF-β1; PICP; MMP-1; TIMP-1; NT-proBNP

title: Hemodynamic Effects of Prophylactic Vasopressors During Anesthetic Induction and Emergency Tracheal Intubation in Adults: A Systematic Review
authors: A. Ali; Sarra Kamil Abbas Mohamed Ahmed; Hanady ME M Osman; Ammar Alemam Diab Alnour; Safaa Mohammed; Yusuf Elmi; Awab Salah Eldin Hassan Elsheikh; Mustafa Eisa Ahmed Elhaj
abstract: Hemodynamic instability is the most frequent serious complication of tracheal intubation in critically ill adults, and prophylactic vasopressors are increasingly used to prevent it.This systematic review assessed comparative evidence on adrenergic vasopressors given before or during anesthetic induction in adults, with emergency tracheal intubation analyzed as a clinically distinct subgroup.Applicability was examined according to clinical determinants of hemodynamic risk, with procedural location, including urgent radiology, considered as one contextual factor.No protocol was registered.Eligibility was broadened from a radiology-specific population to adult induction and emergency intubation in any setting after preliminary searching found no direct comparative studies.PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched for studies published from August 2021 to 15 August 2026, with supplementary searching to 26 September 2026.Risk of bias was assessed with risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2) and Risk of Bias in Non-randomised Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I), and the narrative synthesis followed the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guideline.Of 341 database records, 205 were screened, and 67 full texts were assessed; 13 studies were included (eight randomized, five nonrandomized), one of which was published after the primary database search date.Two studies addressed emergency intubation and 11 addressed planned induction.In planned induction, point estimates mostly favored prophylaxis, but effect sizes ranged from large reductions in moderate hypotension to no difference in severe hypotension (mean arterial pressure below 55 mmHg) in the cardiac surgery trial.The two emergency intubation cohorts were observational and gave discordant results, and no study evaluated intubation for urgent radiology.Benefits for kidney injury and mortality were not shown, and pressure benefits were accompanied in some trials by hypertension or dose-related bradycardia.Prophylactic vasopressors can reduce induction-related hypotension in selected planned-induction populations, but evidence for emergency intubation is limited and conflicting.Emergency status, baseline shock and vasopressor requirement, cardiovascular reserve, and induction technique are more plausible determinants of benefit than procedural location.No universal agent, dose, or regimen can be recommended.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Review Article
authors: Fazila‐Tun‐Nesa Malik; Kalimuddin Md; Nazir Ahmed; Badiuzzman Mohammad; Nesaruddin Ahmed Mir
journal: Journal of National Heart Foundation of Bangladesh
abstract: Over the past two decades, the field of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has undergone significant advancement, driven by both technological innovation and procedural refinement. Once a procedure that was conducted under general anesthesia in an operating room followed by a 5+-day hospital stay is now predominantly being done using moderate sedation in a catheterization laboratory, with many patients being discharged home the following day. Several factors have contributed to this transformation. These include the expansion of TAVR to lower-risk patient populations, reductions in delivery system size facilitating broader use of transfemoral access, and the implementation of streamlined care pathways such as the 3M approach—multidisciplinary, multimodality, but minimalist. This minimalist strategy has been pivotal in enhancing procedural efficiency and reducing resource utilization without compromising outcomes. As a result, TAVR volumes have grown exponentially in recent years and are expected to continue rising, particularly as the procedure is investigated for new indications such as moderate aortic stenosis and asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis. Central to the success of TAVR is a comprehensive assessment of each patient’s suitability for valve replacement, performed by a multidisciplinary heart valve team. Key Wards: Aortic stenosis, transcatheter aortic valve replacement, current situation.

title: Predictors of Early Mortality After Open Aorto-Iliac Reconstruction in Patients with Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: An Observational Cohort Study
authors: Merei Imanbayev; Altay Dyussupov; Bekzhigit Tussupkanov; Ergali Muratzhanov; Ardak Mautbekova; Dinara Kozubayeva; Rustam Mukhametkhanov; Rail Gafurov; Nurbek Irgebayev; Dainius Pavalkis; Evgeniy Zhuravlev; Yersyn Sabitov
abstract: Background and Objectives: Open aorto-iliac reconstruction (AIR) for aorto-iliac occlusive disease (AIOD) remains a high-risk procedure due to multifocal atherosclerosis affecting coronary, cerebrovascular, and renal arterial beds. This study aimed to identify factors independently associated with 30-day mortality and explore factors associated with late mortality during available follow-up among 30-day survivors following open AIR. Materials and Methods: An observational, non-randomised cohort of 170 consecutive patients undergoing open AIR for AIOD between January 2018 and December 2024 was analysed. Univariate logistic regression was performed for 30-day mortality; given the limited number of events (n = 16), the primary multivariable analysis used penalized likelihood logistic regression (Firth correction). Late survival among 30-day survivors (landmark cohort, n = 154) was analysed using Kaplan–Meier methods and exploratory univariate Cox proportional hazards regression, with surviving patients censored at the last available follow-up; multivariable Cox modelling was not performed due to the limited number of late events (n = 10). Results: Thirty-day mortality was 9.4% (16/170) in the overall cohort. In the primary Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression, factors associated with 30-day mortality were: severe left IIA stenosis ≥ 70% (OR 9.68; 95% CI 3.08–30.43; p = 0.0001), chronic kidney disease (OR 3.62; 95% CI 1.03–12.66; p = 0.044), and increasing aortic cross-clamp duration, analysed continuously (OR 1.022 per minute; 95% CI 1.000–1.045); a conventional ≥60 min categorical threshold showed a consistent secondary association (OR 4.15; 95% CI 1.28–13.46; p = 0.018). Non-inclusion of IIA was associated with increased 30-day mortality on univariate analysis (OR 4.80; 95% CI 1.31–17.62; p = 0.018). Among the 154 patients entering the 30-day landmark cohort, 10 late deaths were observed during available follow-up. In exploratory univariate Cox regression, intraoperative blood loss was the only statistically significant factor associated with late mortality (HR 1.07 per 100 mL; 95% CI 1.03–1.12; p = 0.0006). Conclusions: Severe IIA disease, chronic kidney disease, and increasing aortic cross-clamp duration (analysed continuously) were independently associated with increased 30-day mortality after open AIR. Intraoperative blood loss was associated with late mortality in exploratory univariate survival analysis. These findings require validation in larger prospective cohorts with longer and more uniform follow-up.

title: Early applications of apple vision pro in clinical medicine and medical education: a scoping review
authors: Yiwei Hu; Yaqin Wang; Xiaohua Zuo; Haibo Hu; Bo Min; Chengxiang Wang; Chengxiang Wang; Zilong Tang; Ning Xiao; Chenjun Huang; 王储蓄; 王储蓄
abstract: The Apple Vision Pro (AVP), a next-generation spatial computing device, has demonstrated potential applications in multidisciplinary clinical diagnosis, treatment, and medical education, by leveraging its unique technical architecture and performance advantages. In clinical practice, its fundamental advantages of three-dimensional (3D) visualization, real-time image integration, and immersive interaction have been preliminarily employed in disease diagnosis and treatment, surgical planning, precise operations, and postoperative rehabilitation across multiple disciplines. In medical education, AVP surpasses the limitations of conventional models, offering a novel methodology for anatomy education, clinical skills development, specialized practical training, and collaboration of distance learning, thereby alleviating persistent challenges such as unequal distribution of teaching resources, low efficiency in skills and specialized training, and the high cost of distance education. However, AVP faces some limitations, including limited hardware portability, insufficient system compatibility, a lack of specialized medical applications, high costs, and incomplete medical certification. Currently, most evidence derives from feasibility studies, case reports, and opinion pieces. Only two Stage 2b confirmatory studies were identified. Thus, high-level evidence for clinical benefit remains scarce. Readers should interpret all reported benefits as preliminary technical demonstrations rather than established clinical outcomes. Future advancements necessitate iterative development of lightweight hardware design, development of specialized medical software, cross-system optimization, and establishment of standardization protocols. Moreover, more randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and multicenter studies are urgently needed to fully explore and validate its intrinsic value in precision medicine and the equitable allocation of medical resources.

title: Pediatric Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (P-VExUS): a novel approach to assess central venous pressure in the PICU
authors: Fernando de Lima Carioca; Nayara Hillebrand Franzon; Lívia da Silva Krzesinski; Isabel de Siqueira Ferraz; Roberto José Negrão Nogueira; Tiago Henrique de Souza
abstract: Accurate assessment of central venous pressure (CVP) in critically ill children is important for guiding fluid management but remains challenging, as invasive monitoring is not always feasible and noninvasive tools are limited. We aimed to develop and validate pediatric adaptations of the Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (P-VExUS) for bedside estimation of CVP in mechanically ventilated children. This prospective observational study was conducted in a tertiary-care PICU. Fifty-six mechanically ventilated children were included. Venous Doppler ultrasonography of the inferior vena cava, hepatic, portal, and intrarenal veins was performed at the bedside. Two P-VExUS models were evaluated: (1) a categorical grading system (0-III) and (2) a semiquantitative point-based score (0-7). Diagnostic performance was assessed for predefined, clinically relevant CVP thresholds reflecting low (< 7 mmHg) and elevated (> 12 mmHg) venous pressure states using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Both models were significantly associated with measured CVP. For predicting elevated CVP, model 1 showed an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.74 (95% CI 0.61-0.85), with 45% sensitivity and 98% specificity. Model 2 demonstrated superior accuracy (AUROC 0.94, 95% CI 0.84-0.98), with 82% sensitivity and 91% specificity (p < 0.001). For detecting low CVP, model 2 also outperformed model 1 (AUROC 0.80 vs. 0.69; p = 0.02). Intrarenal vein patterns had the highest discriminative ability (AUROC 0.92). CONCLUSION: Pediatric-specific P-VExUS models were feasible and accurate for estimating CVP in critically ill children. The point-based model showed superior diagnostic performance and may represent a promising noninvasive bedside tool for assessing venous congestion. WHAT IS KNOWN: • Elevated central venous pressure (CVP) is associated with adverse outcomes in critically ill children, including mortality and renal dysfunction. • Inferior vena cava-based ultrasound indices have limited accuracy for estimating CVP in mechanically ventilated children, while pediatric adaptations of the Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (VExUS) remain poorly defined. WHAT IS NEW: • This study proposes and evaluates two pediatric adaptations of VExUS, demonstrating superior diagnostic performance of a point-based model for identifying elevated (12 mmHg) and low (7 mmHg) CVP. • Intrarenal venous Doppler showed the highest individual discriminative performance, suggesting potential simplification of venous congestion assessment in critically ill children.

title: A Rare Case of Gorlin-Goltz Syndrome with Multiple Basal Cell Carcinoma Lesions: A Multidisciplinary Surgical Approach
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Gorlin-Goltz Syndrome, also known as nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (NBCCS), is a rare autosomal dominant disorder marked by multiple basal cell carcinomas (BCCs), odontogenic keratocysts, and systemic skeletal anomalies.Early diagnosis is crucial due to the syndrome's potential for multisystem involvement and malignancy risk.This case aims to highlight the clinical spectrum, diagnostic evaluation, and surgical management strategies in a patient with recurrent BCCs in the context of Gorlin syndrome, while emphasizing the role of multidisciplinary care in optimizing outcomes. Clinical Presentation:A case of a 40-year-old Indian male presenting with multiple cutaneous lesions, including ulcerated pigmented nodules, predominantly on the scalp, limbs, and torso.He had a prior history of basal cell carcinoma excisions and a superficial parotidectomy with neck dissection.Systemic evaluation revealed hallmark features of Gorlin syndrome: macrocephaly, frontal bossing, odontogenic keratocysts (on orthopantomogram), and calcification of the falx cerebri (on CECT brain).Wide local excision (WLE) was performed for a symptomatic ulcerated lesion on the left hand.Histopathology confirmed recurrence of BCC.No systemic metastasis or skeletal anomalies were noted, though mild pulmonary arterial hypertension was detected on echocardiography. Conclusion:The case highlights the importance of early recognition and comprehensive management in Gorlin-Goltz syndrome.Multidisciplinary surgical intervention, supported by regular follow-up and systemic evaluation, is essential to prevent complications and recurrence.The case adds to the scarce literature on Indian presentations of Gorlin syndrome and reinforces the need for genetic counselling and vigilant long-term care.

title: Morphological Study of the Tricuspid Valve in Human Embalmed Hearts
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: The tricuspid valve, situated between the right atrium and right ventricle, is a vital component of cardiac anatomy whose morphological variability has significant implications for surgical and interventional cardiac procedures.Anatomical knowledge of its three leaflets-anterior, posterior, and septal-is indispensable for effective valve repair, prosthetic valve design, and understanding functional tricuspid regurgitation.Aims & Objectives: To measure and compare the annular circumference, leaflet length, and leaflet height of the anterior, posterior, and septal leaflets of the tricuspid valve in human embalmed cadaveric hearts, and to establish normative morphometric data relevant to clinical and surgical practice. Materials and Methods:A descriptive cross-sectional anatomical study was conducted at Father Muller Medical College, Mangalore, Karnataka, on 50 embalmed human cadaveric hearts.Annular circumference, valve diameter, and the length and height of each leaflet were measured using a thread-and-scale method and measuring tape.Descriptive statistics including mean, standard deviation, and range were calculated for all parameters.Results: The annular circumference ranged from 8.9 to 15.3 cm (mean ± SD: 11.84 ± 1.42 cm) and valve diameter from 2.83 to 4.87 cm (mean: 3.75 ± 0.48 cm).The anterior leaflet was consistently the largest with a mean length of 4.82 ± 0.83 cm and height of 2.04 ± 0.23 cm.The septal leaflet showed intermediate dimensions, while the posterior leaflet was the smallest and most variable.Conclusion: Significant morphometric variability exists in the tricuspid valve across cadaveric specimens.The anterior leaflet was the largest in all measured parameters, while the posterior leaflet demonstrated the greatest variability.These findings provide normative data of practical value for cardiac surgeons, interventional cardiologists, and biomedical engineers involved in prosthetic valve design.

title: Remimazolam-based total intravenous anesthesia for prone cervical spine surgery in a patient with previously undiagnosed dilated cardiomyopathy after aborted anesthetic induction: A case report
authors: Jooyong Lee; Sanghi Park
abstract: Unexpected hemodynamic deterioration during anesthesia induction may show previously undiagnosed cardiac dysfunction. Herein, we report a case of successful remimazolam-based total intravenous anesthesia in a patient with newly diagnosed dilated cardiomyopathy (DCMP) who underwent prone cervical spine surgery. A 113-kg man with quadriplegia owing to cervical spinal cord injury underwent emergency cervical decompression and fusion surgery. Severe desaturation and hypotension developed despite FiO₂ 1.0 during the initial anesthetic attempt using etomidate and sevoflurane-remifentanil anesthesia, and surgery was aborted. A subsequent evaluation showed DCMP with severely reduced left ventricular systolic function. Reoperation was performed under total intravenous anesthesia with remimazolam–remifentanil. Although transient desaturation and reduced tidal volume developed after prone positioning, surgery was completed with relatively stable hemodynamics. In conclusion, remimazolam-based total intravenous anesthesia may be useful in selected high-risk patients with severe left ventricular dysfunction.

title: Effects of violet light exposure on aging dogs: a pilot study
authors: Kana MIYAMOTO; Nanami Ono; Shinichiro Kondo; Yukihiro Miwa; Kazuo Tsubota; Makiko Ozawa; Takefumi Kikusui
abstract: Aging in dogs is known to induce various physical and brain alterations similar to dementia in humans. Concurrently with the recent extension of canine life expectancy, these age-related changes have imposed growing burdens on both dogs and their owners, emerging as a significant social issue. However, no curative treatment has yet been established, and the current mainstay of management focuses on improving the quality of life through symptomatic therapies, such as environmental modifications and pharmacotherapy. This study focused on violet light, which has suggested efficacy against such age-related changes. We developed a novel violet light irradiation device and evaluated its efficacy and safety in elderly dogs as a pilot study. An intra-individual comparison using an ABA design was employed with geriatric dogs aged 14 to 16 years housed in a senior dog care facility (two of which discontinued midway). The study design consisted of a one-month violet light exposure phase preceded and followed by two-week non-exposure periods. Physical activity levels were measured using accelerometers and cognitive function was assessed using the DISHAA and CCDR. To evaluate the safety, general physical and ophthalmic examinations were conducted by veterinarians. As a result, no significant overall effect was found on activity levels (Daytime: x 2 = 4.22, p = 0.12; Nighttime: x 2 = 1.58, p = 0.45). Similarly, no significant overall effects were observed for either the DISHAA or the CCDR (DISHAA: x 2 = 1.60, p = 0.45; CCDR: x 2 = 1.56, p = 0.46). However, a trend toward cognitive improvement was observed in six out of seven dogs and an upward trend in activity levels-indicating physical function improvement-was noted in two out of seven dogs. Regarding safety, no overt clinical abnormalities associated with violet light irradiation were identified. This pilot study demonstrated no clear overall effect, though some individuals showed signs of improvement. Future research should consider large-scale trials controlling for various variables.

title: Pre-Anesthetic Venous Excess Ultrasound Score for Predicting Spinal Anesthesia-Induced Hypotension in Geriatric Patients Undergoing Elective Lower Body Surgeries: A Prospective Observational Study
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Spinal anesthesia-induced hypotension (SAIH) complications are still prevalent in 16-33% of cases.Objectives: To assess the correlation between the pre-anesthetic venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) grading system and the prediction of SAIH in elderly patients, as well as the correlation between internal jugular vein (IJV) measurements and SAIH prediction in geriatric patients.Methods: This prospective observational investigation included 127 patients aged ≥ 65 years at Tanta University Hospitals over one year.All patients were divided into two groups: Group A (n = 56) with no SAIH and Group B (n = 71) with SAIH.A comprehensive evaluation of prominent systemic veins, including hepatic, portal, renal, and internal jugular veins, was performed on all patients.Results: Delta IJV diameter (ΔIJV-D), delta IJV area (ΔIJV-A), and IJV collapsibility index (IJV-CI) were significantly predictive of hypotension.ΔIJV-D showed an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.697 (P<0.001) at a cutoff >0.11, with 77.46% sensitivity, 57.14% specificity, 69.62% positive predictive value (PPV), and 66.67% negative predictive value (NPV).ΔIJV-A had an AUC of 0.635 (P=0.009) at a cutoff >0.17, with 78.87% sensitivity, 55.36% specificity, 69.14% PPV, and 67.39% NPV.IJV-CI demonstrated an AUC of 0.739 (P<0.001) at a cutoff >19, with 80.28% sensitivity, 76.79% specificity, 81.43% PPV, and 75.44%NPV.Conclusions: Predictors of SAIH in geriatric patients include the simplicity and noninvasiveness of pre-anesthetic IJV-CI, ΔIJV-A, and ΔIJV-D.In contrast, VExUS did not predict SAIH during perioperative assessment.

title: Coronary Artery Disease among Patients Undergoing Valve Replacement Surgery: A Retrospective Study of Angiographic Profiles and Predictors at a Southern Indian Tertiary Care Centre
authors: Gailin Bronson Sebastian; Yokesh Madhavan; Venkatesh Babu; Kiron Sukulal; Jai Arthe; Arya Rajesh; Shreya Gailin; Krishna Viju
journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH
abstract: Introduction: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) frequently co-exists with Valvular Heart Disease (VHD). In developing countries like India, the shifting epidemiology from rheumatic to degenerative VHD alters this association. Concomitant CAD drastically dictates surgical strategies, yet local angiographic profile data remains scarce. Aim: To determine the angiographic profile and clinical predictors of CAD in patients undergoing Coronary Angiography (CAG) prior to valve replacement surgery at an Indian tertiary care centre. Materials and Methods: The present retrospective study was conducted at Sree Mookambika Institute of Medical Sciences, Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu, South India, and analysed data of 200 consecutive patients undergoing preoperative CAG before valve replacement surgery. Demographic profiles, cardiovascular risk factors, echocardiographic parameters, and angiographic findings were reviewed. Patients were stratified into CAD and non CAD cohorts. Obstructive CAD was defined angiographically. Statistical analysis utilised Chi-square and Student’s t-tests. Results: The cohort’s mean age was 55.6±9.3 years; 127 (63.5%) were males (63.5%). Prevalences of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia, and tobacco use were 71 (35.5%), 64 (32%), 30 (15%), and 15 (7.5%), respectively. Patients with CAD were significantly older (mean age: 59.2±8.5 vs 53.8±9.1 years; p<0.001) and predominantly males (72 (73.5%) vs. 55 (53.9%); p=0.005). Increasing age and diabetes mellitus emerged as independent predictors of CAD in multivariate analysis (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.05-1.13; p<0.001 and OR 2.49, 95% CI 1.10-5.63; p=0.028, respectively). No statistically significant association was observed between CAD status and valves involved namely, Mitral Valve Disease (MVD), Aortic Valve Disease (AVD) and combined valve disease or valve surgery performed. AVD showed a non significant trend toward higher prevalence in the CAD group (p=0.11). Left Anterior Descending (LAD) artery was the most frequently diseased vessel {49 (50%)}. Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) was marginally lower in the CAD arm (54.2±12.4% vs 57.1±11.3%; p=0.05), while Atrial Fibrillation (AF) lacked statistical correlation (p=0.89). Conclusion: The CAD in Indian valve replacement candidates was independently associated with advanced age, diabetes mellitus, and standard atherosclerotic risk factors. There was no statistically significant association between presence of CAD and the underlying valve pathology, or the type of surgery performed. Preoperative angiographic screening is critical for precise surgical planning, which should be dictated not only by age but by the presence of cardiovascular risk factors.

title: Translational maturity of artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography varies across cardiovascular diseases
authors: Huanhuan Chen; Jingjuan Huang; Xumin Hou
abstract: Electrocardiography is a widely available and low-cost cardiovascular test, and artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can identify latent electrical phenotypes beyond conventional interpretation. However, high retrospective discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically reliable or actionable benefit. This critical narrative review evaluates the translational maturity of AI-ECG across arrhythmias, acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2022, through July 10, 2026, with earlier landmark studies added by backward citation tracking. Seventy-seven publications informed the review. Evidence was appraised using five clinically oriented criteria: intended use, reference-standard reliability, external validation and transportability, clinical actionability, and effects on workflow or patient outcomes. AI-ECG has progressed furthest in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction triage and reduced-left-ventricular-ejection-fraction screening, where prospective or randomized studies have demonstrated workflow or diagnostic-yield benefits, whereas acute myocardial infarction rule-out has reached prospective multicenter diagnostic validation. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy screening has also advanced through international validation and prospective implementation. By contrast, occlusion myocardial infarction detection, prediction of occult or future atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, long-term heart-failure prediction, and cardiac amyloidosis remain primarily validation-stage or risk-enrichment applications. Across domains, broader adoption is constrained by label quality, calibration, transportability, operating-threshold selection, and limited patient-outcome evidence. AI-ECG is therefore best positioned as clinician-supervised decision support linked to explicit downstream testing and care pathways.

title: PREECLAMPSIA AS A WINDOW INTO FUTURE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE: PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL LINKS, LONG-TERM RISK, AND POSTPARTUM PREVENTION
authors: Rodolfo de Oliveira Medeiros; Feres Abrão; Lorrana de Sousa Landim Xavier; Rodrigo Hara Ariosa; Kellen de Pícoli Alexandre; Hellen Cristine Nunes Gonçalves; Laura Rodrigues Albuquerque; Késia Letícia Scombate; Ana Lídia Correia dos Santos; Eduardo Antônio Ferro Faria; Ana Luiza de Souza; Cynthia de Paula Costa Borba; Luisa Magalhães Rodrigues; Thalles Eduardo Silva Santos; Ana Laura Jorge Manzini; Gabriel Francisco Alves; Wanderson Dieikon Xavier Da Silva; André Marciano Neto; Henrique Felipin Da Silva Evangelista
abstract: Preeclampsia is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy that affects a substantial proportion of pregnancies and remains a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity. Beyond its immediate obstetric consequences, a growing body of evidence indicates that women with a history of preeclampsia carry a higher long-term risk of chronic hypertension, ischemic heart disease, heart failure, stroke, and cardiovascular death. Shared risk factors, endothelial dysfunction, antiangiogenic imbalance, and vascular and myocardial changes that persist after delivery may explain this association, which allows pregnancy to be interpreted as an early cardiovascular stress test. At the same time, the history of preeclampsia is still inconsistently recorded in clinical practice, and postpartum follow-up is often fragmented between obstetric and primary care. This review aimed to analyze preeclampsia as a window into future cardiovascular disease, considering the pathophysiological links, the magnitude of long-term risk, and the opportunities for postpartum prevention. This is a narrative literature review, guided by a structured question based on the PICo strategy and directed at studies on the cardiovascular trajectory of women with a history of preeclampsia. The evidence shows a roughly twofold increase in the risk of coronary heart disease, a higher risk of heart failure and stroke, and an earlier onset of chronic hypertension, with a gradient according to the severity, timing, and recurrence of the disorder. Much of the excess risk appears to be mediated by conventional risk factors that emerge in the years following delivery, which favors early detection. Postpartum interventions targeting blood pressure have shown promising results, although evidence on hard cardiovascular outcomes is still lacking. It is concluded that preeclampsia should be incorporated into cardiovascular risk assessment, with structured postpartum follow-up and continuity of care throughout the female life course.

title: Anesthesia Management in Pregnant Women with Cardiac Disease: A Narrative Review
authors: Berrin Günaydın; Nuray Camgöz Eryılmaz; Gözde İnan
abstract: This review addresses the perspective of an obstetric anesthesiologist, focusing on the practical principles of peripartum anesthetic management by integrating current evidence with contemporary guideline recommendations rather than providing a comprehensive overview of cardiovascular disease during pregnancy. It also provides a clinically oriented approach to hemodynamic optimization, delivery planning, neuraxial and general anesthetic management, and the treatment of obstetric cardiac emergencies. Ultimately, this review aims to answer the question every anesthesiologist faces in daily practice: “What should the anaesthesiologist do for cardiac pregnant patient?” Cite this article as: Gunaydin DB, Camgoz Eryilmaz N, Inan G. Anesthesia management in pregnant women with cardiac disease: a narrative review. Eurasian J Med. 2026, 58(4), 1693, doi: 10.5152/eurasianjmed.2026.261693.
